title: check-skill-name-drift.mjs — unify three lexical drift guards (HIGH LEVERAGE)
description:
Deferred from SWARM-39 (item #35) and flagged there as the highest-leverage of the three.

Unifies what are currently three separate concerns: the M4 Set-vs-disk skill-name check, stale command references, and stale comments. Vocabulary is self-updating from readdirSync(skills/), scanning code, shell and markdown surfaces.

Load-bearing prior result: four ast-grep agents PROVED these are LEXICAL, not structural — prototypes hit 80-94 percent false positives when written as ast-grep rules. So this must be a JS check over collected text (lib/mdast.mjs collectScannableText already does the prose/fenced split), NOT a bespoke .ast-grep rule. That negative result is the main reason this bead is worth its priority: the cheap-looking implementation is known to fail.

Real precedent for what it would have caught: SWARM-39's own H1 finding was three recovery strings still naming /package-intel and /tool-intel after the rename to /intel — functional breakage that a green npm run check was blind to.

Build in fresh context per the adversarial-review-before-shipping rule.

Source: SWARM-39.md, deferred checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- A skill renamed on disk without updating its references fails npm run check.
- The vocabulary derives from readdirSync(skills/), never a hardcoded list.
- False-positive rate on the existing tree is zero (the check passes on main before any fix).
- Implemented as a JS check, not an ast-grep rule — with the 80-94 percent FP finding recorded in the code.

title: Link-integrity audit pipeline: enumerate, classify, repair, report dangling wiki-links
description:
The graph carries ~1,246 unresolved relations of 13,109. A 2026-07-29 sampling
session established this is NOT one backlog but four populations needing
opposite treatment:

1. REPAIRABLE - target note exists, link text wrong. Five observed modes:
   permalink slug pasted; em-dash vs hyphen; colon vs hyphen; short-form title
   (dominant); case. Root cause is the house title convention
   "Concept Name - Long Descriptive Subtitle" while authors link the concept.
2. FORWARD-REF - no such note. Deliberate markers. Leave; rank as /intel candidates.
3. SPURIOUS - not a link at all. Per vp-claude-dpz6 a [[wiki-link]] in prose or
   observation context is silently extracted as a relation. Never "repair" these.
4. PLACEHOLDER - illustrative links inside schema/template notes.

Feasibility probes (2026-07-29) settled the design:
- `bm tool search-notes --permalink "main/*" --entity-type relation --page-size 1000`
  enumerates relations as JSON; rows lacking `to_entity` are the unresolved set.
  ~14 paginated calls covers the graph at zero model cost.
- `bm tool` has NO relations query and NO list-directory; search-notes `content`
  is TRUNCATED mid-note, so literal link text must come from `read-note`.
- Resolution appears to be exact-title, not slug equality (a hyphen-vs-em-dash
  link slugified identically to its target and still dangled) - pin with fixtures.

Deterministic matching against a one-shot title index replaces N fuzzy searches
- the thing that made cheap-tier classification unreliable (~50% wrong in both
directions across 10 sampling agents).
acceptance_criteria:
- lib/link-resolution.mjs: pure slugify + strategy-ordered matcher + classifier emitting canonical bucket strings
- scripts/list-unresolved-links.mjs: paginated `bm tool` enumeration -> NDJSON
- scripts/check-link-resolution.mjs wired as `npm run check:link-resolution`, fixture-covering every observed failure mode plus spurious/placeholder exclusion
- Bucket strings shared gardener<->maintainer, guarded like staleness-contract
- Report ranks forward-refs by DISTINCT source-note count, not raw edge count
- Repairs dry-run by default with a resumable manifest

title: feature-nudge slash-command evidence check is unsatisfiable against real dispatch data
description:
## Summary
Live production run of the just-released 0.31.10 fix found 0/15 catalog features show confirmed evidence, even though several (/goal, /fork, /advisor, /fewer-permission-prompts) are demonstrably in heavy real use. Root cause confirmed with 600 real samples across all 54 project directories: the slash-command evidence check requires a <command-name> tag match AND promptSource:"typed" AND origin.kind=="human" together, but a genuine dispatch entry's message object is ALWAYS exactly {role, content} -- no promptSource, no origin, no permissionMode field ever exists on a real dispatch (0/600 samples had either). The check is backwards: it requires fields that are absent on every genuine case while present on ordinary prose.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run /feature-nudge for real against ~/.claude/projects with real transcript history containing genuine slash-command usage
2. Observe every feature reports 0 confirmed sessions despite genuine usage existing in the transcripts

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replace the promptSource/origin.kind requirement with the structural check confirmed via 600-sample investigation: type==="user", message.content is a string (not array), the string (trimmed) starts with <command-name> or <command-message>, and the top-level entry carries none of toolUseResult/sourceToolAssistantUUID/requestId
- Re-verify both directions: the corrected check finds real dispatches (false-negative fix) AND still excludes the self-contamination cases already found this session (false-positive regression check)
- Ship as its own patch version (0.31.11), tag + push
close_reason: Fixed: replaced the unsatisfiable 3-field check (tag + promptSource:typed + origin.kind:human) with two structural dispatch shapes confirmed against 600 real samples. Shape A: type:user, string content starting with the tag, no tool_result markers. Shape B (newly discovered mid-fix via live dogfooding /fork): type:system/subtype:local_command, content directly on the entry -- confirmed as the general emission shape for every built-in local command (/fork, /exit, /mcp, /doctor, /plugin, /model, and others), not a one-off. Verified in both directions: real dispatches for /goal, /advisor, /fewer-permission-prompts, /fork now correctly detected; both known self-contamination cases (assistant tool-call args, tool-result forwarding) still correctly excluded. Shipped 0.31.11, tagged and pushed (b602e01).

Results: (1) /nudge-sync full workflow run against the REAL BM note -- fetch, slug-uniqueness check, filter, write -- all correct, content matched exactly (all 15 features unseen, none excluded). (2) hooks/session-start.sh run for REAL (not a fixture) -- first run today correctly surfaced a tip ('goal'), second same-day run correctly throttled, state file correctly written. title: fix(package-intel): append-mode places observations after ## Relations
description:
Three of three recent npm notes from /package-intel (npm-umzeption, npm-@voxpelli-pg-utils, npm-@yikesable-fastify-saas-auth-pg) show trailing observations bleeding past the ## Relations section into end-of-file.

## Symptom

BM parses everything between ## Relations and EOF as the Relations section, so trailing observation lines containing [[wiki-links]] produce malformed relations with ~300-char relation_type strings (the prose preceding the wiki-link). Indexed observation count drops below file body count.

Concrete: npm-umzeption has 22 indexed observations vs ~27 in the file body — 5 silently dropped. One produces a ~300-char relation_type overflow on a [[npm-umzug]] edge.

Affected notes (2026-05-19 audit):
- npm-umzeption — 5 orphan observations after ## Relations
- npm-@voxpelli-pg-utils — 9 orphan observations
- npm-@yikesable-fastify-saas-auth-pg — 1 orphan [feature]

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick an npm package that already has a Basic Memory note (e.g. npm-umzug or any /package-intel output).
2. Run `/package-intel npm:<pkg>` a second time on the same package (update path).
3. `read_note(identifier="npm-<pkg>", output_format="json")`.
4. Observe: new observations appear in file body AFTER `## Relations`, not appended to `## Observations`.
5. Run `schema_validate(note_type="npm_package")` — note the malformed relation_type entries containing observation prose.

## Root cause hypothesis

/package-intel's update path uses `edit_note(operation=append)` without targeting the `## Observations` section. BM's `append` + `section` parameter goes to end-of-file regardless (documented gotcha in CLAUDE.md), so the skill must use `find_replace` at an anchor inside `## Observations` instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- skills/package-intel/SKILL.md update step uses `edit_note(find_replace)` anchored at the last line of `## Observations` (not `append`).
- Same fix applied to skills/tool-intel/SKILL.md if it shares the bug pattern.

title: intel Step 6: the completeness check can silently never run
description:

That is the exact failure the new text warns against, one level up: the instruction to report a silent skip is itself silently skippable.

Deliberately deferred at the time — it touches the Step 6 contract and deserves design, not another same-session patch.

Source: docs/design/intel-corrections-2026-07-28.md, Part 2 finding 1.
acceptance_criteria:
- Step 6 has an explicit bullet requiring the completeness check's own status, separate from the changelog source's status.
- Reporting 'changelog: used' without a completeness-check verdict is no longer a well-formed Step 6 report.

title: Fix the 9-rule bucketing fallthrough bug immediately, not defer
description:
## Decision

Fixed a real pre-existing bug in knowledge-gardener.md's 9-rule version-drift
bucketing model (rules 2/2b) in the same session it was discovered, as part
of the /knowledge-gaps --stale plugin epic, rather than filing it and shipping
the plugin cohort with a documented known limitation.

## Rationale

The bug (a not-in-api/api-unavailable note with a parseable recorded version
fell through to the versions-differ rules, comparing against an empty
upstream_version string and landing in a nonsensical "Drifted, age unknown"
bucket) was discovered via live end-to-end dogfooding of the new plugin
cohort, but is cohort-agnostic -- it could affect any past --stale run across
brew/npm/cask/crate/vscode too. The fix is small, provably safe (it only
rescues notes that previously fell through to a wrong bucket; it cannot
break a case that currently routes correctly), and directly affects the
correctness of the very report this epic ships. Deferring would mean
knowingly shipping a cohort whose most common outcome (not-in-api, 13/18 of
the Anthropic marketplace) was verified to sometimes mis-render.

## Alternatives Considered

- File separately, ship plugin cohort as-is with a documented known
  limitation in the not-in-registry prose. Rejected -- the fix was small and
  safe enough that deferring would have been avoiding a 10-minute fix rather
  than genuinely managing scope.

## Affects

agents/knowledge-gardener.md Step 5b-iv (rules 2/2b), and by extension every
past/future --stale or knowledge-gardener Step 5b audit across all six
cohorts. Follow-up: vp-claude-gfxv audits whether any already-recorded
--stale result was affected by the pre-fix behavior.

title: audit existing --stale results for the newly-fixed 9-rule bucketing bug
description:
Fixed 2026-07-04 (agents/knowledge-gardener.md Step 5b-iv rules 2/2b): a
not-in-api or api-unavailable note with a PARSEABLE recorded bm_version
previously fell through the 9 ordered bucketing rules to the versions-differ
comparison, landing in a nonsensical "Drifted, age unknown" bucket instead of
"Not in registry"/"API unavailable". Verified via classifyVersionDistance
('1.0.0', '') -> 'distance-unknown'. Discovered via the new plugin cohort's
end-to-end dogfooding run, but the root cause is cohort-agnostic -- brew,
npm, cask, crate, and vscode could all have hit this same fallthrough in any
PAST --stale run or knowledge-gardener audit, wherever a not-in-api/
api-unavailable note also had a parseable recorded version (e.g. a renamed/
removed package whose note still records last-known version cleanly).

## Acceptance Criteria

Re-run knowledge-gardener Step 5b (or /knowledge-gaps --stale, all cohorts)
against the real graph and confirm no note is currently mis-bucketed as
Drifted/age-unknown that should be Not-in-registry/API-unavailable under the
corrected rules. If any are found, no note content needs fixing (the bug was
in report RENDERING/classification, not stored data) -- just confirm the
NEXT real audit run reflects the corrected bucketing.

title: lib/installed-plugins.mjs: git-subdir source drops the separate path field
description:
Confirmed via live verification (2026-07-04) against two real marketplaces
while building the --stale plugin fetch script: a {source:"git-subdir", url,
path, ref} marketplace entry carries its in-repo subdirectory in a SEPARATE
`path` field, not encoded inside `url`. Real examples:
- databricks/databricks-agent-skills: {"source":"git-subdir","url":"databricks/databricks-agent-skills","path":"plugins/databricks/claude","ref":"main"} -- url here is even just bare owner/repo shorthand, not a URL.
- hugohe3/ppt-master: {"source":"git-subdir","url":"https://github.com/hugohe3/ppt-master.git","path":"skills"}

lib/installed-plugins.mjs's PluginSource typedef (line 57) and its git-subdir
branch (line 183, ownerRepoFromUrl) only read `url`, silently dropping `path`.
This affects the existing `/knowledge-gaps --global` plugin-coverage feature
-- any git-subdir plugin whose subdirectory isn't the repo root either
resolves to the wrong (repo-root) location or falls back to the unresolved
identifier form, never locating the actual plugin.json.

The NEW scripts/fetch-plugin-upstream.sh (this session, bd vp-claude-uzd6)
does NOT have this bug -- its own resolve_source() was written independently
and correctly reads .path, plus handles the bare-owner/repo url shorthand.
Verified end-to-end against databricks/databricks-agent-skills#databricks:
resolves to plugins/databricks/claude/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, fetches
version 0.2.9 correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Find a marketplace.json entry with {source:"git-subdir", path: "<non-root>"}
2. Run /knowledge-gaps --global against an install using that plugin
3. Observe the resolved identifier/coverage record ignores the path field

## Acceptance Criteria

lib/installed-plugins.mjs's PluginSource typedef and git-subdir branch read
and use the `path` field; check-list-installed-plugins.mjs fixture tests
cover a git-subdir entry with a non-root path.
close_reason: Fixed narrower than originally scoped: resolveInstalledPlugins never fetches repo content (only builds a plugin:<owner>/<repo>#<name> identifier for BM-note matching), so a missing 'path' field alone doesn't corrupt current behavior — the fixture data already carried path in git-subdir test fixtures without asserting on it, confirming this was a known, deliberate omission, not an oversight. The REAL confirmed bug: ownerRepoFromUrl's regex required a literal 'github.com' substring, silently failing on the bare 'owner/repo' shorthand url shape (verified real-world: databricks/databricks-agent-skills). Fixed lib/installed-plugins.mjs's ownerRepoFromUrl to accept both shapes; added a regression-guard fixture case + typedef comment explaining path is deliberately uncaptured here (fetch-plugin-upstream.sh is the consumer that needs it). npm run check green.

title: Phase 0 blind-spot verification + end-to-end run for --stale plugin
description:

path-derivation against a fresh non-BM-documented multi-plugin marketplace
that DOES version its plugin.json files, or (b) manually confirm by eye that
the derived path for a known anthropics plugin (e.g. code-review ->
plugins/code-review, per that note's own [source] observation) matches what
the algorithm computes.

Then: end-to-end /knowledge-gaps --stale plugin run against the real graph
(impeccable, ast-grep plugin, vp-knowledge/vp-beads/vp-git resolve correctly;
anthropics notes report not-in-api not a false "current" or a crash; report
omits Archive candidates; S8 footnote lists plugin as supported). Finish with

run output reviewed; npm run check green.
close_reason:
Phase 0 (marketplace path-resolution): confirmed correct via live verification against real, non-Anthropic multi-plugin marketplaces (databricks/databricks-agent-skills git-subdir with separate path field, ast-grep/agent-skill self-hosted with a subdirectory source) -- both bare-repo and marketplace-resolved paths verified against production GitHub data with exact version matches.

End-to-end run: all 22 real plugin-* BM notes processed through the actual fetch-plugin-upstream.sh script and bucketed via the corrected 9-rule model. Result: 1 Drifted >30d (vp-knowledge, semver-major escalation from the 0.x minor-bump rule), 2 Drifted <30d (impeccable [semver-minor-multi], security-guidance [patch]), 13 Not in registry (Anthropic marketplace members confirmed version-less), 6 Current. Zero Unparseable, zero Archive candidates (correctly omitted per no-deprecation-flag design), zero API unavailable.

Two significant findings from actually dogfooding the workflow (not caught by static review):
1. Corrected an overgeneralization in 4 doc locations + 1 script comment: version-presence is per-PLUGIN not per-marketplace (13/18 Anthropic plugins are version-less, 5 have real versions) -- the original plan text wrongly implied the whole Anthropic marketplace is uniformly version-less.
2. Found and fixed (with user approval) a real pre-existing bug in knowledge-gardener.md's 9-rule bucketing model: a not-in-api/api-unavailable note with a PARSEABLE bm_version fell through to the versions-differ rules, comparing against an empty upstream_version string and landing in a nonsensical 'Drifted, age unknown' bucket instead of 'Not in registry'/'API unavailable'. Verified against the real classifyVersionDistance('1.0.0', '') -> 'distance-unknown'. Fixed both the not-in-api and the analogous api-unavailable per-note cases in one pass.

Also refined S3's identifier-recovery logic after discovering vp-git's real-world shape: a plugin's own url:/[source] repo can carry its own root plugin.json while ALSO being referenced by an unrelated third-party aggregating marketplace -- naively concatenating them produces a wrong marketplace lookup. Added explicit disambiguation (marketplace.json != plugin.json) after a targeted user flag.

title: tool-intel/package-intel: guard against CHANGELOG Unreleased-section tag-lag mis-attribution
description:
## Background

Real mis-attribution found and corrected 2026-07-03 in `brew-sem-cli` during a
`/tool-intel` upgrade haul (sem-cli 0.16.2 -> 0.17.0, llmfit 0.9.36 -> 0.9.37).
The existing note attributed `sem orient --pack` and an attention-ledger
"delta-fill" enhancement to v0.16.2. `gh api compare/v0.16.2...v0.17.0` proves
both actually shipped in v0.17.0 (exactly 3 commits: #449/#450/#451-452);
v0.16.1->v0.16.2 itself contained only a rustfmt tweak and an MCP-registry
namespace-casing fix.

Root cause: `Ataraxy-Labs/sem`'s `CHANGELOG.md` hand-cuts its `## [Unreleased]`
section into versioned headers on a slower cadence than it cuts git tags. At
correction time the newest cut header was still `## [0.15.1]` while tags
already ran through `v0.17.0` -- four releases ahead. Reading `Unreleased`
prose for feature attribution during that gap silently blends multiple
releases together with no boundary markers between them, and nothing in the
current package-intel/tool-intel changelog step (SKILL.md Step 3d /
`references/gh-api-fallback.md`) flags this gap before trusting the content.

This is a generic risk for any repo with a hand-maintained (non-automated,
e.g. not release-please) CHANGELOG -- not specific to sem-cli.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Document a check (in `gh-api-fallback.md`, shared by both package-intel and
  tool-intel) that compares the newest CHANGELOG.md version header against
  the newest git tag before trusting `## [Unreleased]` prose for single-version
  feature attribution
- When a lag is detected (cut header behind the newest tag), require deriving
  the changelog for the affected version(s) from `gh api
  compare/<tagA>...<tagB>` commit ranges instead of the Unreleased prose
- Name this as a reusable gotcha/pattern alongside the existing "git tag ahead
  of GitHub Release" and "empty release body" gotchas already documented for
  this class of repo
- Cross-reference the concrete motivating case: brew-sem-cli v0.16.2/v0.17.0
  mis-attribution, corrected 2026-07-03
close_reason: Documented a CHANGELOG cut-lag gotcha (compare newest CHANGELOG.md version header vs newest git tag before trusting Unreleased prose; fall back to gh api compare for affected versions) in both package-intel and tool-intel gh-api-fallback.md, cross-referencing the brew-sem-cli v0.16.2/v0.17.0 mis-attribution.

title: Version bump for 0.32.1: patch over minor despite a fourth-wall-hook precedent argument
description:
## Decision
0.32.1 (patch) chosen over 0.33.0 (minor) for the release covering 9 commits since 0.32.0, including the fourth-wall detector's runtime hook wiring.

## Rationale
None of the 9 commits are "breaking" by this project's own stated bar (compare to 0.22.0's disruptive colon-to-hyphen migration). The fourth-wall hook wiring is a genuine new automated behavior on every write_note/edit_note call, comparable in kind to the knowledge-maintainer refresh-queue redefinition that justified 0.32.0's own minor bump -- this was presented as the strongest argument for minor. User chose patch instead: a stricter reading that treats "genuinely breaking" (not just "user-visible new behavior") as the minor-bump bar.

## Alternatives Considered
- 0.33.0 (minor) -- rejected. Would have followed the 0.32.0 precedent's logic but the user explicitly preferred a stricter breaking-changes-only bar for minor bumps.

## Affects
Sets precedent for future borderline cases: a new automated hook/check that changes observable behavior on every relevant tool call is NOT automatically minor-bump-worthy on its own -- only genuinely breaking changes (API contract changes, required migrations, removed capabilities) warrant minor under this project's semver convention. Future release-checklist judgment calls should default to patch unless a change is disruptive enough to need a migration note, not just "new behavior users will notice."

title: knowledge-prime/knowledge-maintainer: wrong recent_activity pagination (has_more doesn't exist)
description:
## Description

`recent_activity` has no `has_more` field and returns a flat top-level
`result` array (singular key, not nested under `results`) -- verified live
against the actual MCP tool, including with `page_size=1`/`page_size=2`
against cohorts with more items than one page, and confirmed returning
duplicate rows per entity across pages. This is a different shape from
`search_notes`, which genuinely does return `{results, current_page,
page_size, total, has_more}`.

Two occurrences of this bug were already fixed in SWARM-33 wave 1's
post-gate fix cycle (2026-07-02): `skills/knowledge-gaps/references/
staleness-detection.md` S1 and `agents/knowledge-gardener.md` Step 5 (Stale
note detection). A fresh re-gate pass on that same wave found the pattern
survives in at least one more place, out of that wave's file scope:

- `skills/knowledge-prime/SKILL.md:111` -- "Paginate until `has_more=false`
  to ensure complete 7-day activity window" immediately after a
  `recent_activity(timeframe="7d", ...)` call. An agent following this
  instruction literally has no valid loop-termination signal.

Also flagged as worth tightening (LOW, same root cause):

- `agents/knowledge-maintainer.md:797` ("Efficient Tool Usage" section)
  generalizes "Set explicit `page_size` and paginate with `page` +
  `has_more`" without scoping it to `search_notes` specifically -- the same
  file calls `recent_activity` at Step 1.4 (line 207) without a caveat, so a
  reader could misapply the `has_more` pattern there. Contrast with the
  equivalent line in `knowledge-gardener.md`, which explicitly names
  `search_notes`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call `mcp__basic-memory__recent_activity(timeframe="7d",
   output_format="json", page_size=2)` against a project with more than 2
   recent items.
2. Inspect the response shape: top-level key is `result` (singular), and no
   `has_more` field exists anywhere in the payload.
3. Compare against `skills/knowledge-prime/SKILL.md:111`'s instruction to
   "paginate until `has_more=false`" -- the described termination condition
   never fires.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skills/knowledge-prime/SKILL.md:111` corrected to the same
  page-increment-until-short-page mechanic used in the two already-fixed
  files (no `has_more` check; flat `result` array; dedup guidance if this
  spot also cross-references `read_note` results the way the other two do).
- `agents/knowledge-maintainer.md:797`'s generic pagination line either
  scoped explicitly to `search_notes` (matching `knowledge-gardener.md`'s
  phrasing) or given an explicit `recent_activity` exception.
- `npm run check` passes after the edits.
close_reason: Fixed wrong recent_activity has_more pagination guidance in knowledge-prime/SKILL.md:111 and scoped the has_more pagination line in knowledge-maintainer.md:797 to search_notes with a recent_activity exception, matching the wording already fixed in staleness-detection.md and knowledge-gardener.md

title: upgrade-haul: resolve Axis-B target to a linked timeline note when one exists
description:
## Problem

The tool-intel upgrade-haul adapter hardcodes its Axis-B narrative target to
"inline `[feature]`/`[version]` observations in the tool's own note"
(skills/tool-intel/SKILL.md, *Adapter: tool-intel surface* point 3). This
misroutes when a high-velocity tool's changelog has been **extracted to a
dedicated timeline note** — the subject note keeps only standing facts and a
`see_also`/`documented_in [[... Release History]]` relation pointing at the
extracted note.

Discovered 2026-07-02 during a `/tool-intel`-style upgrade haul
(`brew upgrade claude-code@latest sem-cli deno clevercloud/tap/clever-tools
biome`): `Claude Code Release History` was split out of `cask-claude-code` the
day before (2026-07-01). Run blindly, the haul would have appended the new
changelog reel back into the cask note, re-inflating exactly what had just
been extracted. Handled as a manual one-off override for that haul; this bead
tracks generalizing the fix into the skill itself.

## Proposed fix

Before writing Axis B, the adapter should check the subject note's Relations
for a linked timeline note (a `see_also`/`documented_in` relation whose target
title matches a "... Release History"/timeline pattern) and, when present,
append the curated reel there instead of inline. Axis A (the version pipe/slot)
always stays in the subject note regardless. Fall back to today's inline
behavior when no linked timeline note exists.

Touches:
- `skills/tool-intel/SKILL.md` — *Adapter: tool-intel surface* point 3 (Axis-B
  narrative target)
- `skills/package-intel/references/upgrade-haul.md` — *Per-skill adapter
  contract* (Axis-B narrative target requirement)

Future candidates for the same extraction pattern: deno, biome (both
high-cadence release notes currently inline).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skills/tool-intel/SKILL.md` documents the linked-timeline-note check as
      part of the Axis-B routing step, with a worked example
      (`cask-claude-code` → `Claude Code Release History`)
- [ ] `skills/package-intel/references/upgrade-haul.md`'s *Per-skill adapter
      contract* section reflects that Axis-B target resolution can be
      relation-driven, not just a fixed section/inline convention
- [ ] `npm run check` passes after the doc edits
- [ ] Dogfooded on at least one future haul touching a note with an extracted
      timeline note (or manually verified against the `cask-claude-code` /
      `Claude Code Release History` pair)
close_reason: Documented the linked-timeline-note check for Axis-B routing in tool-intel SKILL.md (cask-claude-code → Claude Code Release History worked example) and generalized the Per-skill adapter contract in upgrade-haul.md to allow relation-driven Axis-B target resolution.

title: feature-nudge Step 2: Glob's file-return ordering doesn't reliably surface the most-recent transcripts across many projects
description:
## Summary
Discovered via live dogfood verification (bd vp-claude-elrr.7.7). feature-nudge's Step 2 says: Glob(pattern="**/*.jsonl", path="~/.claude/projects"), sort by mtime descending, take the top ~50. This works correctly when the result set is small, but across ~4142 real transcript files spanning many projects, a dogfood run found the "top 50 by mtime" were all subagent transcripts from an unrelated project (md-wiki-vec, dated 2026-05-27 to 2026-06-16) -- NOT the current live session, which was actively running at the time and had a top-level transcript file with mtime "Jul 1 12:28" (today), unambiguously more recent.

Root cause hypothesis: Glob itself appears to cap/truncate its returned result set (confirmed separately: "100 of 4141 matching files; 4041 more not listed") in a way that isn't a true global mtime sort before truncation -- so the skill's own "sort by mtime, take top 50" instruction only sorts among whatever arbitrary subset Glob's cap happened to include, not the true freshest 50 across all 4142 candidates. This means feature-nudge's evidence-gathering can systematically miss the user's own most-recent, most-relevant session while over-indexing on whatever project's files happen to fall inside Glob's own internal cap.

Confirmed via a real dogfood run (2026-07-01): of 15 seeded feature slugs, only "cd" (a generic shell command, not a distinctive feature) showed real evidence in the top-50 window; every other slug returned 0, and several near-misses were false-positive text collisions (e.g. "advisor" matching "advisories", "sandbox" matching a ubiquitous JSON schema field name) that the skill's own criteria correctly excluded, but the deeper problem is the wrong 50 files were being examined in the first place.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Have many project directories under ~/.claude/projects, several with large subagent-transcript bursts (many .jsonl files from background/subagent activity)
2. Run feature-nudge's Step 2 exactly as documented: Glob(pattern="**/*.jsonl", path="~/.claude/projects"), take the mtime-sorted top ~50
3. Observe that the resulting file list may not include the actual most-recently-modified session/subagent files across the whole ~/.claude/projects tree, especially when total file count is in the thousands

## Acceptance Criteria
- Determine why Glob's file-return set doesn't reflect a true global mtime sort at scale (or confirm/refute this hypothesis with a smaller controlled test)
- Redesign Step 2's file-selection strategy so it reliably captures the CURRENT project's own most-recent activity, not just whatever falls inside an arbitrary cap when scanning across all projects -- candidate approaches: scope the primary scan to the current project's own directory first (cheap, small, definitely correct) before/in addition to a cross-project sweep; or explicitly read+sort mtimes client-side rather than trusting Glob's own ordering
- Re-run the live dogfood verification after the fix and confirm real evidence surfaces for at least one feature genuinely used in the current session (e.g. /goal, /advisor, /fork -- all used extensively in this same session)
close_reason: Fixed: replaced Glob-based mtime pre-filter with direct content search (Grep, no recency-window pre-filter). Root cause: Glob's ~100-file cap applies traversal-order truncation, not a true mtime sort, so the actively-running session could be silently absent from the computed 'recent 50'. Two independent Plan-agent explorations (robust multi-stage vs simplicity-first) both required a never-before-used CWD-to-sanitized-project-dir mapping; an advisor review found a simpler synthesis -- per-slug content Grep is inherently correctness-complete regardless of file ordering, since a feature's mentions are sparse relative to any practical cap. Implementation additionally fixed two gaps the plan review caught before coding: (1) search terms are now derived from each tip's own backtick-quoted invocation syntax, not the machine-only normalized slug nobody types; (2) shape-check now requires a whole-word match, closing a real false-positive class the original dogfood run hit ('advisor' matching 'advisories'). A distinct fresh-install case (~/.claude/projects not existing) is now handled separately from a genuine tool/path failure -- confirmed empirically that a missing directory throws a 'Path does not exist' error, not a clean zero-match result. Live-dogfooded post-fix (not just statically checked): confirmed the current session's own transcript is now reliably found in evidence-gathering for two real slugs (fixing the exact regression), and confirmed the shape check correctly declines to treat mere discussion of a feature as adoption evidence (a stronger validation than a lucky positive match would have been). Shipped as 0.31.8, npm run check clean except the pre-existing unrelated check:md issue. Committed b43b0e7.

comments.author: Pelle Wessman
comments.text:
BLOCKED — premise disproven, no code changes made.

The issue assumes Claude Code's skill router reads a `when_to_use` frontmatter field in addition to `description`. Verified via claude-code-guide agent against the official Agent Skills docs (platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview#skill-structure): only `name` and `description` exist in the spec, and `description` alone drives auto-invocation routing. There is no second routing field.

Corroborating signal already in-repo: validate-plugin.mjs's SKILL_KNOWN_FIELDS allowlist (the fields this plugin actually recognizes/uses) does not include `when_to_use` either — both the external spec and the internal convention agree it isn't real.

I added the field to both SKILL.md files, ran `npm run check` (passed, with two new "Unknown skill frontmatter field" warnings — expected since the field isn't in SKILL_KNOWN_FIELDS), then reverted both edits before closing out: shipping an inert field would satisfy the acceptance-criteria checklist literally while leaving the actual goal (keyword-less batch lines auto-routing) unmet and undiscoverable until someone hits it live.

Decision needed: the only real routing surface is `description`. To make keyword-less batch lines (`npm outdated`, `brew upgrade foo bar`) auto-route, the batch trigger phrases would need to go into `description` itself — which conflicts with this issue's explicit "do NOT lengthen description" constraint (tool-intel's is already ~1018 chars). Options: (a) accept some description growth and pick a length budget, (b) find a different mechanism (e.g. a SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hook that pattern-matches pasted upgrade lines and suggests the right skill, rather than frontmatter-based auto-routing), or (c) drop the auto-route goal and rely on users invoking the skill explicitly for batch mode. Needs a human call — reopening/leaving in_progress rather than closing.

- Delta-reel convention (unit of work = recorded→installed version delta): sem-cli 0.13.0→0.14.1, uv 0.11.23→0.11.24, glab 1.102.0→1.105.0, biome 2.5.0→2.5.1, llmfit 0.9.31→0.9.33, claude-code 2.1.185→2.1.187. Each got a curated changelog reel (skip merges/internal refactors), not a commit dump.
- Two-axis recording confirmed in practice: Axis A = machine `[version]` observation (had to bump llmfit's HEADLINE [version] stamp separately — Release Highlights alone left the top-of-note version stale, a concrete gotcha the shared reference should call out: refresh BOTH the headline [version] obs AND the narrative); Axis B = prose reel (inline [feature]/[version] for tool-intel).
- Batch orchestration: 6 file-disjoint research subagents in ONE message, no API-burst throttle (sat right at the documented ~4-6 cap edge and was clean). Writes centralized in the main context (not delegated to subagents) to dodge the edit_note inline-count echo gotcha.
- Stale-cache arbitration, concrete edge case: claude-code is a CASK, so fetch-brew-upstream.sh returned upstream_state="not-in-api" (formulae.brew.sh is core-only). Had to dispatch to fetch-cask-upstream.sh. The shared upgrade-haul.md adapter (1bf9) MUST name formula-vs-cask auto-routing on a not-in-api signal, and glob BOTH brew/ and casks/ in the Step-1 existence check — exactly as 1bf9's AC already states.

Two genuine breaking/behavior changes surfaced that a bare `brew upgrade` would hide: glab orbit --format→--response-format (breaking), biome LSP go-to-definition now off-by-default (memory-leak fix). This is the value proof for the highlights-reel: catching silent behavior changes.

Net: design validated. When mz69 reaches "dogfood before tagging", this run is the reference trace.

title: Explore an 'adoption' dimension (notable users) for the *-intel commands
description:
## Context

While researching `npm-vscode-extension-tester` (ExTester), GitHub code search over `package.json` (`gh search code '"vscode-extension-tester"' --filename package.json`) surfaced recognizable adopters — Microsoft (.NET Aspire, vscode-fabric, Azure LogicAppsUX), Docker, Continue, Oracle, Intel, MathWorks, Amazon Ion, IBM OpenLiberty, Trail of Bits, plus the maintainer's own extensions. This 'who notably uses it' signal is a strong credibility/relevance cue that none of the current seven package-intel sources capture. Recorded ad hoc as an `[adoption]` observation on that note.

This is the same shape as vp-claude-5b6 (added Socket depscore as a 7th source).

## Scope to explore

- **package-intel**: GitHub code-search of dependents' manifests (`package.json`/`Cargo.toml`/`go.mod`/`composer.json`/`requirements.txt`/`Gemfile`) -> curated list of recognizable-org adopters. Per-ecosystem manifest + dep-field differs (deps vs devDeps).
- **tool-intel**: distinct mechanic per prefix — Actions: search `.github/workflows` usages; brew/cask: install analytics already cover this (don't duplicate); docker: harder (no manifest); vscode: marketplace install counts already exist. Decide which prefixes the dimension actually adds signal for.
- **people-intel**: arguably already covered (notable projects/affiliations) — assess overlap before extending.

## Open questions

- Curate aggressively (recognizable orgs only) vs dump — code search returns 40+; need a relevance heuristic (org reputation, star count?).
- `gh search code` rate limits + auth requirements; degrade gracefully when unavailable (like Socket/Raindrop empty-source handling).
- Schema: formalize an `[adoption]` observation category in the package/tool schemas (dual-sync), or keep it freeform.
- Provenance convention: end the observation with `(GitHub code search, YYYY-MM)` as the context field (verified safe — no markdown-link-plus-parenthetical drop).
- Source-count propagation if it becomes a numbered source (CLAUDE.md 'seven-source', README, skill prose, CHANGELOG).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide whether 'adoption' becomes a formal numbered source, an optional sub-step, or stays an ad-hoc observation pattern
- [ ] If adopted: package-intel Step 3 documents the code-search procedure with a curation heuristic and graceful-degradation rule
- [ ] If adopted: per-prefix decision recorded for tool-intel (which prefixes gain signal, which already have it)
- [ ] If adopted: `[adoption]` category + provenance convention added to relevant schemas and dual-synced
- [ ] Source-count strings propagated if it becomes numbered, OR a note explaining why it stays unnumbered
close_reason: Dropped, not implemented: the ~6-schema + 2-skill surface cost (formalizing an [adoption] observation category, per-prefix tool-intel decisions, source-count propagation) isn't worth it for a signal that's speculative (curation heuristic undecided, gh search code rate-limits). Revival trigger: revisit only if a concrete consumer need appears — e.g. a person/tool note where 'who actually uses this' is load-bearing for a real decision, not just trivia. Decided during SWARM-36 planning, 2026-07-03.

title: people-intel emits aliases: frontmatter (bare name) on new person notes
description:
## Context

people-intel writes notes titled "Name - Descriptor". Other notes link them by bare [[Name]], which BM resolves only by exact title -> dangling edges (116 graph-wide, concentrated on people; the Pelle Wessman note has 4 dangling bare-name edges vs 97 resolved full-title). Emitting a bare-name aliases: entry on the descriptive note makes [[Name]] resolve in Obsidian now, in any md-wiki-vec index claiming Obsidian-compat, and in BM once its LinkResolver gains an alias step.

The alias approach DOMINATES retargeting each link: one alias on the target resolves all present+future bare links (O(1), links stay natural) vs rewriting each link to the verbose full title (O(N)).

INERT-IN-BM CAVEAT (document in SKILL.md): BM STORES aliases: but does NOT resolve against it today (LinkResolver cascade has no alias step). Inside BM tooling a [[bare name]] click stays dead until the upstream resolver fix lands -- do not misread that as broken. Value is realized in Obsidian / md-wiki-vec now, BM later.

Scope: focused emit only (people-intel, going-forward). NO schema change -- schema_validate does not check YAML frontmatter (confirmed empirically: a note with aliases validates 0 warnings). NO backfill (that is vp-claude-wehg territory). package/tool-intel use bare npm-x/brew-x titles -> out of scope.

Relations: relates_to vp-claude-wehg (reconcile/backfill sibling fork); relates_to the upstream LinkResolver item in UPSTREAM-basic-memory.md. NOT blocked by the upstream issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- people-intel emits aliases: ["<Full Name>"] in the frontmatter of every new person note -- the name component already used to build the "<Full Name> - <Descriptor>" title (no title-string-splitting; the skill has the name). Values are bare strings in a YAML list, never wrapped in [[ ]].
- MAY include >1 alias when a commonly-linked variant exists (handle, full given name); the full name is always present.
- SHOULD skip the alias (and note it) if the bare name already exists as another note title or alias, to avoid an ambiguous Obsidian target.
- SHOULD: the "Existing person" update path adds aliases when absent (frontmatter find_replace anchored on the title: line, never crossing a --- fence), so re-runs self-heal -- without a bulk backfill.
- NO schema change and NO dual-sync (frontmatter is not schema-validated). Optionally add a one-line [convention] to schemas/person.md ## Conventions documenting the alias rule -- documentation only, NOT a picoschema field.
- SKILL.md documents the alias is inert inside BM tooling today, resolves in Obsidian / md-wiki-vec now, BM later, with a pointer to the upstream LinkResolver item.
- npm run check passes; a test new person note shows aliases persisted (read_note json) and validates clean.
close_reason: Implemented in 2d1ab2f: people-intel emits aliases: frontmatter (template + SKILL Step 4 + self-heal SHOULD). No schema change needed (frontmatter unchecked, verified). npm run check green; end-to-end persist+validate confirmed.

title: package-intel Step 5 overwrite path drops relations and leaves a stale permalink
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. /package-intel on a package whose BM note already exists as an older/non-conforming stub at a DIFFERENT directory or title (e.g. an indieweb/history stub for what is now an npm package).
2. Step 5 takes the write_note(overwrite=True) path.
3. read_note the result by its expected new permalink.

## Expected
Note carries the correct permalink for its new ecosystem location; genuine relations from the old stub are preserved.

## Actual
Overwrite silently DROPS the old note's real relations (observed: a used_by edge) and keeps the OLD frontmatter permalink (file at npm/X.md, permalink still indieweb/history/...). write_note(overwrite) and move_note both preserve the explicit permalink; only a direct edit_note(find_replace) on the permalink line re-keys it. See UPSTREAM-basic-memory.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Step 5 overwrite branch re-keys the permalink to match the target ecosystem dir+title
- [ ] Genuine relations from the prior note are carried forward (read old note first) or the user is warned about dropped edges
- [ ] Documented in the skill + MEMORY.md (overwrite is not a fresh create)
close_reason: Documented the relocated-stub overwrite procedure in package-intel Step 5: search broader than the directory-scoped glob, read the stub's old relations+permalink before overwriting, carry forward genuine relations into the new write, and re-key the permalink via edit_note(find_replace) since write_note(overwrite) and move_note both preserve the old permalink verbatim.

title: Basic Memory FTS text-search recall failure — 0 hits for strings present in notes
description:
During the Sprint 32 Fable-5 graph-impact sweep (2026-06-09), a research agent found Basic Memory full-text search returning zero results for strings that demonstrably exist in notes. This makes coverage audits (/knowledge-gaps, knowledge-gardener) unreliable — they can silently miss affected notes.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Note `cask-claude-code` contains the literal strings "Opus 4.8", "Mythos", and "Fable" (verified by read_note).
2. Run `search_notes(query="Opus 4.8", search_type="text")` — returns 0 results.
3. Run `search_notes(query="Mythos OR Fable", search_type="text")` — returns 0 results.
4. Run `search_notes(query="Opus", search_type="text")` — result set omits `cask-claude-code`.
Hybrid search partially compensated but did not surface all known matches.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Root cause identified (suspected: stale/lagging FTS index — `cask-claude-code` was created/edited 2026-06-08/09, so recently-written notes may not be indexed yet; confirm whether `bm sync`/reindex resolves it).
- Either a reindex fixes recall, OR the workaround is documented (audits must triangulate text + hybrid + filesystem grep, not trust text search alone).
- knowledge-gaps / knowledge-gardener docs note the limitation if not fixed upstream.

title: Backfill version slots promote-verified-only, not backfill-all
description:
## Decision
When backfilling a machine-stable [version] slot, stamp ONLY notes whose recorded version is verifiable against a trusted anchor (GitHub/GitLab/Repo header pipe, **Latest**:, existing [version] obs, frontmatter). Stale/drifted/unparseable notes acquire the slot on their next /package-intel or /tool-intel refresh instead.

## Rationale
Stamping a stale recorded number makes the note disagree with itself. Stamping the current upstream version zeroes-out drift detection (bm == upstream forever). The verify-each gate caught yaml (1.1 from a spec feature-table cell) and semver (5.0.0 from a range example) false positives that an automated backfill would have durably persisted; schema_validate passing does not catch a well-formed wrong value.

## Alternatives Considered
- f3zx original "backfill ~200 in batches": rejected -- includes inaccurate notes.
- Stamp upstream-latest everywhere: rejected -- kills drift detection.
- Forward-emit only, no backfill: rejected -- leaves the existing corpus prose-parsed indefinitely.

## Affects
vp-claude-f3zx and all future package/tool cohort version-slot work; /package-intel and /tool-intel emit rules; the new tool-cohort task filed this sprint.
close_reason: Decision implemented in 0.31.4 promote-verified-only 71-note backfill; verified against CHANGELOG

title: deep-intel B3: fail-closed verification routing — agent-routed VERIFY_TOOL_ROUTING_PROMPT
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
PROBLEM: verification currently hardcodes 'Use ToolSearch to load mcp__tavily__tavily_search' in 5 places (adv:HIGH, confirm:HIGH, adv-batch, confirm-batch, and the macro/judge area uses Tavily as sole verify backbone). Tavily-as-sole-verifier is a single point of failure (vqow.14 resilience rationale) and ignores the claim's own cited URLs.

- Replace the 5 hardcoded mcp__tavily__tavily_search verify strings with a shared VERIFY_TOOL_ROUTING_PROMPT that routes in ORDER:
  1. extract from the claim's own cited source URL(s) (injected into the prompt — pass each obs/claim's source URLs to its verify agents),
  2. mcp__tavily__tavily_search (web cross-check),
  3. Basic Memory (mcp__basic-memory__search_notes) as an additional cross-check source.
- NO Bash anywhere in the verify agents.
- On tool-load failure (e.g. an MCP tool cannot be loaded), the agent returns NO_EVIDENCE_FOUND — fail-closed, never a silent CORROBORATED. This preserves the rollup invariant (NO_EVIDENCE_FOUND + confirm = single-source hedged, never cross-checked).
- Inject the claim's source URLs into both the adversarial and non-adversarial verify agents (HIGH per-claim pair AND the MEDIUM/LOW batched pairs).
- Document the routing order + fail-closed contract in references/verification-topology.md.
- npm run check green.
- DEPENDENCY: INDEPENDENT of the B1->B2->B6 chain (can land in parallel). Soft-depends on the model-tier bead (vqow.19) since verify agents calling MCP must be sonnet+ (the HIGH-stake adv/confirm are already sonnet; the adv-batch/confirm-batch are haiku and MUST be re-tiered — see vqow.19).
- Operationalizes the fail-closed + verification-routing finding in vqow.14 (parent finding).
notes: WEB-TIER REFINEMENT (user): the web-corroboration option in the routing prompt is BUILT-IN WebSearch/WebFetch, not mcp__tavily. Ordered preference: claim-cited-URL via WebFetch -> WebSearch for breadth -> BM (mcp) for graph-internal. Built-ins avoid the ToolSearch/allowlist/Haiku friction; reserve MCP for curation/authoritative cross-checks.

title: knowledge-gaps: detect installed Claude plugins + skills.sh skills as tool-coverage gaps
description:

- skills.sh skills: ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ directory enumeration, each with SKILL.md (analogous to .vscode/extensions.json)

So the "no manifest" exclusion that legitimately covers gh: does NOT hold here. Every other auto-detectable tool ecosystem has BOTH halves (manifest detector in knowledge-gaps + research in tool-intel); plugin/skill currently have only research, so an undocumented plugin/skill never surfaces as a gap.

Caveat to resolve during impl: these manifests are USER-GLOBAL (~/.claude), not project-local like Brewfile/.vscode. Decide whether plugin/skill detection belongs in the per-project Step 6 sweep or behind an explicit flag (e.g. --tools=global), to avoid every project audit reporting the same global plugin set. Likely a separate opt-in detector, not the default project glob.

## Acceptance Criteria
- knowledge-gaps can enumerate installed Claude plugins (installed_plugins.json) and skills.sh skills (~/.claude/skills/*/) and cross-reference against BM claude_plugin notes
- Undocumented plugins/skills surface in the Tool Coverage Report with /tool-intel plugin:/skill: bootstrap invocations offered
- Global-vs-project scoping decided and documented (default does not spam project audits with the global plugin set)
- description trigger-phrase list + .claude/rules/skill-development.md knowledge-gaps inventory updated to mention plugin/skill detection
- gh: remains excluded (genuinely has no manifest) -- documented as the deliberate contrast case

title: vscode staleness picks pre-release over stable (CalVer shadows semver)
description:
Surfaced refreshing vscode-biomejs.biome (2026-05-29). scripts/fetch-vscode-upstream.sh reads Open VSX .version, which is the highest-SORTING version — and a CalVer pre-release (2026.3.311859) sorts ABOVE a semver stable (3.6.1). biome-vscode runs two concurrent channels (stable=semver, pre-release=CalVer), so the registry latest IS the CalVer pre-release. The '/knowledge-gaps --stale vscode' check compared documented stable 3.5.0 against the pre-release latest and emitted a false [semver-major] drift. See BM notes CalVer (tooling-hazard section) and vscode-biomejs.biome.

Two defects:
1. fetch-vscode-upstream.sh picks the pre-release as upstream_version. It should prefer the latest NON-pre-release version. Open VSX /api/<pub>/<ext> returns .version + a .preRelease bool; the versions list at /api/<pub>/<ext>/versions (paginated) has no stable-only filter — likely walk versions picking the highest with preRelease=false, or add an openvsx_prerelease bool to the NDJSON for the bucket logic to skip.
2. staleness-detection.md + knowledge-gardener 2-D model: a semver<->calver SCHEME MISMATCH (one side parses YYYY.x, other MAJOR.x with small major) must resolve to distance-unknown, never a false semver-major escalation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a vscode note documenting a semver stable version (e.g. biome 3.x).
2. Run /knowledge-gaps --stale vscode (or gardener Step 5b vscode cohort).
3. Observe the note flagged Drifted >30d with [semver-major] against a 2026.x CalVer pre-release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- fetch-vscode-upstream.sh resolves upstream_version to the latest non-pre-release Open VSX version (or emits a preRelease flag the consumer uses to skip) so biome resolves to 3.6.1 not 2026.3.311859
- A semver<->calver scheme mismatch resolves to distance-unknown (never semver-major) in both staleness-detection.md and knowledge-gardener Step 5b
- A regression check (fixture or documented manual probe) covers the mixed-scheme case
- npm run check passes
notes:
ARCHITECT BLUEPRINT (code-architect, 2026-05-29). Approach: lazy stable resolution in fetch-vscode-upstream.sh. Open VSX default /api/<pub>/<ext> body carries versionAlias [latest,pre-release] + full allVersions map (all keys, NOT paginated) + per-version .preRelease. No 'stable' alias exists. Logic: if default .preRelease==false → upstream_version=.version (0 extra cost). If ==true → parse allVersions keys from the ALREADY-FETCHED body, filter out CalVer (leading numeric component >=2000) + alias keys, sort semver desc, take top, ONE confirming GET /api/<pub>/<ext>/<ver> to verify preRelease:false + get timestamp. Emit additive openvsx_prerelease bool; upstream_version=resolved stable (biome→3.6.1), openvsx_version=raw .version (provenance). Pre-release-only ext (no stable found) → upstream_version=pre-release, openvsx_prerelease=true → consumer applies scheme-mismatch guard.

Scheme-mismatch guard (distance model): CalVer = leading component >=2000. If one side CalVer and other not → distance-unknown, gating rule 5 BEFORE it can fire semver-major. Both-CalVer stays comparable (year bump=semver-major, correct). 18→19 not misread (both <2000).

FILES (7): (1) scripts/fetch-vscode-upstream.sh — extract_stable_version() + openvsx_prerelease NDJSON field; (2) skills/knowledge-gaps/references/staleness-detection.md S3 (compute drift against upstream_version NOT openvsx_version) + S4 (distance-unknown row gains scheme-mismatch clause; escalation-rule scheme guard; vscode per-cohort note; cohort table upstream-version cell); (3) agents/knowledge-gardener.md Step 5b-iv (rule 5 prerequisite scheme guard; distance table; per-cohort; cohort table); (4) NEW lib/version-distance.mjs (pure classifyVersionDistance); (5) NEW scripts/check-version-distance.mjs (biome case = fixture #1); (6) package.json check:distance wired into run-p check:*; check:contract UNCHANGED (bucket strings untouched).

IMPLEMENTATION BUGS TO AVOID (flagged by main agent, not design flaws): (a) typo $ovenvsx_is_prerelease in one emit call → $ovsx_is_prerelease; (b) '[[ -z ]] && echo "" && return' is fragile under set -e (failed && list as standalone statement trips errexit) — restructure to if/then.

VERIFY: printf biomejs.biome | bash fetch-vscode-upstream.sh → upstream_version 3.6.1, openvsx_prerelease true; S4 yields [patch] not [semver-major]; node check-version-distance.mjs all pass; npm run check green. Full blueprint in agent transcript.

title: fix(scripts): git-tag date fallback in fetch-brew-upstream.sh Tier-2 timing
description:
The Tier-2 enrichment block in scripts/fetch-brew-upstream.sh (~L139-149) reads release timing via `gh release list --json publishedAt`. For formulae that tag releases but never cut a GitHub Release (e.g. brew:sem — formula stable 0.6.0, git tag v0.6.0, but `gh release list` topped out at v0.5.5), this leaves days_stale=null and tier="1", so brew version drift is under-reported by knowledge-gardener Step 5b.

Companion to the v0.30.1 skills-only change (release-list staleness heuristic + git-tag fallback in /tool-intel and /package-intel). Deferred from that change to keep the markdown-only edit separate from shellcheck/shfmt-validated code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When `gh release list` returns empty/no publishedAt for an active repo, the script falls back to the newest git tag's commit date via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/tags --jq '.[0].commit.committer.date'` (or equivalent) to compute days_stale
- Tier-2 classification works for tag-without-release formulae
- Script still passes shellcheck + shfmt (npm run check:sh)
- Provenance of the fallback date is distinguishable in output (tag vs release) if practical
close_reason: Added git-tag commit-date fallback in fetch-brew-upstream.sh Tier-2 block when gh release list is empty, plus a new days_stale_source field (release|tag|null) for provenance

title: Context7 MCP resolve-library-id rejects both libraryName and query parameters
description:
The Context7 MCP server's `resolve-library-id` tool is broken in both parameter directions, making it impossible to call successfully. Triggered three times in Sprint 26 on umzeption, npm-run-all2, and the @rjsf trio during /package-intel runs.

## Symptom

- Passing `libraryName="X"` errors: `Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at path `query`
- Passing `query="X"` errors: `Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at path `libraryName`

The parameter schema is internally inconsistent — there is no valid invocation. The skill prose says to use `libraryName` per the canonical example.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Invoke `mcp__claude_ai_Context7__resolve-library-id` (or the equivalent in another Context7 server install) with `libraryName="npm-run-all2"`.
2. Observe error complaining `query` is missing.
3. Retry with `query="npm-run-all2"`.
4. Observe error complaining `libraryName` is missing.

## Workaround

`/package-intel` and `/tool-intel` skills both have explicit "skip Source B if it returns no useful result" branches. They handle the failure cleanly — the bug is detectable but recoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either: file upstream against the Context7 MCP server (likely `upstash/context7` or `@anthropic-ai/context7`)
- Or: add a workaround note to `skills/package-intel/SKILL.md` and `skills/tool-intel/SKILL.md` documenting that resolve-library-id is currently broken
- Or: create `UPSTREAM-context7.md` and log the entry there
- Decision recorded in this issue when triaged
close_reason: Created UPSTREAM-context7.md tracking the resolve-library-id parameter-schema bug (rejects both libraryName and query) with repro steps and the existing skill-level fallback workaround; no GitHub issue filed per scope restriction

title: upstream basic-memory: edit_note(append, section=X) appends to EOF, not section end
description:
## Summary

Basic Memory's `edit_note(operation="append", section="<name>")` ignores the `section` parameter and appends to end-of-file regardless. The API accepts a `section` argument but doesn't honor it.

## Impact in this project

Drove `vp-claude-fo8` (the /package-intel update-path bug). Three npm notes were silently damaged (observations placed below `## Relations` and parsed as malformed relations with ~300-char `relation_type` overflows).

## Proposed upstream fix

Make `section` constrain the append target — append to the end of the named section, not the file. Deprecating `section` for append (the alternative) would break back-compat with existing callers.

## Workaround in this project

Skills use `edit_note(operation="find_replace")` anchored on the last observation line. Documented in `session-reflect/SKILL.md` lines 127-143 and (after fo8 lands) in the three intel skills.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Upstream issue filed against `basicmachines-co/basic-memory` repo
- Issue promoted to `UPSTREAM-basic-memory.md` via `/upstream-tracker`
- Once fixed upstream and released: the workaround prose can be removed from the three intel skills

## Source

Discovered 2026-05-19 via /package-intel append-mode bug investigation (vp-claude-fo8).

- Direct Edit on schemas/*.md
- Targeted mcp__basic-memory__edit_note(find_replace) inside YAML block on BM picoschema notes

title: [bug] knowledge-maintainer Section 3b: minimal version bumps lose signal vs full /tool-intel
description:
Sprint 23 field-test of v0.29.3 staleness chain revealed that Section 3b 'auto-batch up to 5 /tool-intel brew:<name> refreshes for Drifted >30d' executes as minimal version bumps (single `[release]` observation) when run in unattended/background mode, NOT as full 5-source /tool-intel enrichments.

The agent rationalized this as 'Skill tool only loads instructions on parallel invocation, not enrichment loops' and applied edit_note with version-only updates for cosign, git-delta, shfmt.

Concrete signal loss: cosign 3.0.5 → 3.0.6 looked like a routine patch bump but actually patches THREE 2026 CVEs (CVE-2026-22703 bundle verification bypass, CVE-2026-39395 auth bypass, CVE-2026-24122 cert chain timing). All three were captured ONLY when a subsequent manual /tool-intel brew:cosign ran the full 5-source pipeline.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Stage a brew note (e.g. brew-cosign) with a recorded `[version]` observation behind the current upstream version such that the gardener Step 5b bucketing places it in Drifted >30d.
2. Run /knowledge-gardener (or invoke directly) so it emits the canonical `### Brew Version Drift` section.
3. Run /knowledge-maintainer in background mode (via Agent tool, run_in_background=true) with the gardener report as input.
4. Inspect the maintainer's actual edits to the >30d targets — observe single `[release] vX.Y.Z` line additions rather than full 5-source enrichment.
5. Compare against a manual /tool-intel brew:<same-name> run; the manual run surfaces multiple [security]/[architecture]/etc. observations the minimal-bump path missed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either: maintainer Section 3b spawns /tool-intel subagents recursively for each Drifted >30d target (concurrency capped at 5 per documented behavior).
- Or: maintainer Section 3b is redefined as 'queue these names for main-session action' and the agent emits a structured queue rather than acting itself.
- Either way: security-sensitive tools (any with prior `[security]` observation) ALWAYS get full /tool-intel regardless of age bucket — would have caught the cosign case.
- Update knowledge-maintainer.md prose to match the chosen behavior so users do not see a documentation/behavior mismatch in unattended mode.
close_reason: Redefined knowledge-maintainer Section 3b as a queue (not an actor): Drifted >30d targets are emitted into a Refresh Queue report for the human-supervised foreground session to action, never bumped via edit_note or via recursive Skill-tool spawning; security-flagged targets (prior [security] observation) always land in a distinct HIGH PRIORITY/IMMEDIATE ACTION queue lane regardless of age bucket.

title: /tag-sync should backfill missing blocklist on pre-seeding vocab files
description:
## Why

skills/tag-sync/SKILL.md Step 2 (lines 67-68) seeds "blocklist" on creation; Step 8 (lines 177-179) preserves user config across syncs. The live ~/.claude/references/raindrop-tags.md was created BEFORE the seeding step landed, so its frontmatter has tag_count + fetched_at + mandatory_tags but NO blocklist field. Sync mode preserves what it finds, so the field never backfills — stale-creation-mode-output bug.

Tolerance fallback in skills/raindrop-triage/references/tag-selection.md Step C (lines 22-27) is graceful but lossy: numeric tags + "imported" only, missing the curated for:*/toread/unread/readlater bans that the audit identified as ~526 bookmarks of legacy noise.

This gates vp-claude-rgw quality (iterative-elicitation track) and any future raindrop-triage / raindrop-gardener invocations against the user library.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read ~/.claude/references/raindrop-tags.md frontmatter
2. Confirm absence of blocklist, context_tags, conventions fields
3. Run /tag-sync (sync mode against the existing file)
4. Observe: file is updated with tag count and fetched_at refresh, but the missing seed fields are NOT backfilled
5. Run /raindrop-triage on a fixture containing for:*/toread/etc. tags
6. Observe: those tags are not blocked despite being intended-by-design blocked entries

## Resolution

Modify skills/tag-sync/SKILL.md Step 8 to additively heal: when sync mode encounters a vocab file missing blocklist / context_tags / conventions, populate those fields with the Step-2 seed values WITHOUT touching present user-curated entries. Source: Sprint 21 wave-2 multi-agent research.

title: Document 'gh' as explicit fallback in /package-intel and /tool-intel when DeepWiki and Context7 return empty or wrong
description:
## Why

Sprint 19 ran /package-intel on go:github.com/timakin/bodyclose. DeepWiki returned hallucination-class wrong answers (info about noctx and go-critic instead of bodyclose); Context7 had no Go indexing. The recovery — pivoting to `gh api` for raw README + go.mod + commits + issue/PR state + contributor list — produced eight gap-fills across one note and salvaged the run.

This pattern is durable but currently invisible in the skill prose:

- /package-intel SKILL.md Step 3 lists DeepWiki, Context7, Tavily, Raindrop, Readwise, changelog, Socket. No mention of `gh` as a structured-data alternative when DeepWiki/Context7 fail.
- /tool-intel SKILL.md Step 3 has similar omission. The action: prefix already uses `gh release list` for changelog, so `gh` is partially in scope, but as a "use this tool" directive, not as a structured fallback when other sources go bad.

Captured in BM as a [pattern] in the BM tool catalog ("`gh api` is the structural fallback when DeepWiki and Context7 produce unreliable or empty output for a target repo"), but the skill prose is the read path for every future run — observation in BM doesn't propagate without skill prose update.

## What

1. /package-intel SKILL.md — add a sub-step or note to Step 3 explicitly listing the `gh` API endpoints worth trying when sources a (DeepWiki) and b (Context7) return empty or repo-mismatched answers:
   - `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<path>` — README, manifest, source files
   - `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits` — change history
   - `gh issue view <n> --repo <r> --json state` — issue freshness verification
   - `gh pr view <n> --repo <r>` — PR ground truth
   - `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contributors` — maintainer profile
2. /tool-intel SKILL.md — same addition, scoped to action:/gh:/docker: prefixes (the GitHub-rooted ecosystems where `gh` is most useful).
3. Cross-link to the BM tool catalog [pattern] from skill comments where appropriate.
4. Mention specifically that DeepWiki has a hallucination-class failure mode (returning info about a *different* repo) — confidence in DeepWiki output requires repo-name verification, especially for small/personal repos.

## Acceptance

- Both /package-intel and /tool-intel SKILL.md mention `gh api` as a structured-data fallback with concrete endpoint examples
- The "verify cited issue is OPEN" pattern is documented as a [pattern] step in the synthesis workflow (currently only in BM enrichment-pattern note)
- A test run of /package-intel against a niche repo confirms the prose makes the fallback obvious before the user has to think of it

## Notes

Related: vp-claude-sav (UPSTREAM-deepwiki.md decision) is about *tracking* the friction; this bead is about *mitigating* the friction in the skill workflow itself. Both should land before the next Sprint-19-style failure mode recurs.

- The "verify cited issue is still OPEN" pattern is referenced as a [pattern] step in the synthesis workflow, not just in the BM enrichment-pattern note
- Test run of /package-intel against a niche Go or non-npm repo confirms the gh fallback prose makes the alternative path obvious before the user has to think of it

title: /knowledge-gaps: use 'brew leaves' as ground-truth for installed formulae
description:
Currently /knowledge-gaps parses Brewfile which is aspirational; we want to diff against what is actually installed. Surface "installed but not in Brewfile" (silent deps worth documenting) and "Brewfile entries not installed" (dead declarations).

IMPLEMENTATION (revised 2026-05-05 after multi-agent research):

Use Bash + `brew leaves` (already available; ~200ms; returns leaf-only formulae directly), NOT mcp__homebrew__list. Three reasons the original design fails:

1. mcp__homebrew__list returns plain text (one name per line) without `installed_on_request` metadata — cannot distinguish leaves from transitive deps from this output.
2. Per-formula leaf detection via mcp__homebrew__info would need ~190 calls × 2-5s each = 6-15 min — unacceptable.
3. `brew leaves` is the canonical leaf-finder (per BM Homebrew API Data Availability Matrix) and runs in ~200ms total.

Bash is already in /knowledge-gaps allowed-tools, so no allowlist update is needed.

Spawned from Homebrew MCP integration plan (vp-claude-baz). YAGNI-revive: when user runs /knowledge-gaps and asks "why isn't jq flagged?" because jq is installed but not Brewfile-declared.
acceptance_criteria:
- Workflow diffs Brewfile entries against `brew leaves` output (via Bash) and surfaces both directions:
  - Installed-but-not-Brewfile-declared (silent deps worth documenting)
  - Brewfile-declared-but-not-installed (dead declarations)
- `brew leaves` is the data source (NOT `brew list` which includes transitive deps; NOT per-formula mcp__homebrew__info which is too slow)
- Test run with a known silent dep (e.g., jq installed without Brewfile entry) confirms it is flagged in the appropriate category
- Fallback when `brew` CLI is not installed: skip the diff and emit Brewfile-only behavior without errors

title: Quantitative claims in the intel corrections have no reproducible artifact
description:
'18 of 502 npm notes', '7 of 330 version bumps across 42 formulae', '6 of 40 null-head formulae', '120 of 120 sampled formulae' live only in comments and commit messages. Verifying any of them means redoing the scan from scratch.

This matters more than usual here, because one of these measurements was already wrong once in exactly this way: a partial 318-of-502 scan was reported as complete ('8 multi-[version] notes'; real figure 18), and a separate count was inflated by 5 read failures that grep -c reported as genuine zeros.

Two acceptable outcomes: commit the scan scripts, or soften the claims to what is re-derivable.

Source: docs/design/intel-corrections-2026-07-28.md, Part 2 finding 4 and Part 4.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every load-bearing quantitative claim in the corrections either has a committed script that reproduces it, or is restated without the precise figure.
- A scan that fails to read a note reports the failure; it never emits 0.

title: intel brew: no stated fallback when the bare-name analytics key is missing
description:
ecosystem-brew.md tells the agent to read the bare-name analytics key but says nothing about what to do if it is absent.

Bounded, not urgent: a reviewer tested ~15 formulae spanning very-low-traffic, pure-dependency and renamed cases and COULD NOT produce a real miss, and a later sample found the bare-name key present in 120 of 120 formulae. So this is theoretical rather than observed.

Worth one line anyway, because the wrong recovery is attractive: an agent that cannot find the bare-name key may substitute the --HEAD variant, which measures a different population.

Source: docs/design/intel-corrections-2026-07-28.md, Part 2 finding 3.
acceptance_criteria:
- ecosystem-brew.md states what to do when the bare-name key is absent (treat as 0 and say so).
- It explicitly forbids substituting the --HEAD variant.

title: intel: guard the hardcoded 'seven behaviors' count in gh-api-fallback.md
description:
`skills/intel/references/gh-api-fallback.md:89` says "seven GitHub API/CHANGELOG behaviors" and there are exactly seven bullets — correct today, unguarded tomorrow.

The count was changed from five to seven when two bullets were added (2026-07-28). A hardcoded count adjacent to an edited list is a classic rot point: the next person to add a bullet has no reason to look at the header, and no check in `npm run check` counts them.

This is the same class `check:release-counts` already guards for CLAUDE.md/README component counts — the mechanism exists, it just does not cover this file.

Source: docs/design/intel-corrections-2026-07-28.md, Part 2 finding 13.
acceptance_criteria:
- Either a check counts the bullets and fails on mismatch, or the prose stops naming a number.
- If a check: it lives with the other drift guards and is wired into `npm run check`.

title: README/manifest first-contact clarity pass (naive-reader findings)
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

From the v0.32.2 pre-release naive-reader review pass (2 independent naive skill-reviewer + 1 naive plugin-validator agents). Communication-clarity findings, none release-blocking, all real friction for a genuinely fresh reader:

title: knowledge-maintain skill: add target-resolution step, wire 3 phantom tools, close dangling-relation + schema-drift gaps
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

Confirmed by 2 independent pre-release reviewers. knowledge-maintain (the skill, not the agent) lacks the target-resolution step its sibling knowledge-garden has:
- search_notes, build_context, list_directory are declared in allowed-tools but never called in workflow prose (phantom-tool violation, one-directional so npm run check doesn't catch it)
- No prefix-to-directory / topic-search resolution path (garden has one), so fuzzy input like /knowledge-maintain brew:ripgrep has no defined path to the actual note title
- Step 4 "Add a relation" appends relates_to [[target]] WITHOUT verifying the target resolves first (dangling-relation risk) -- build_context could close this
- Schema-note edits through this skill can silently drift from schemas/*.md (skill has no Edit tool, no dual-sync instruction) -- needs a carve-out routing picoschema-definition edits to /schema-evolve, or an explicit scope boundary

- [ ] Decide: add a garden-style resolution step (wire the 3 tools live) OR commit to exact-titles-only (drop the 3 tools, tighten description/argument-hint)

- [ ] Add schema-note edit scope boundary (route to /schema-evolve, or explicitly exclude schema notes)
- [ ] Fix description wording: "confirms each edit" overstates -- Step 3's auto-fix column applies without confirmation
- [ ] npm run check green
close_reason: Wired search_notes/build_context/list_directory into knowledge-maintain's new Step 2 target-resolution (mirroring knowledge-garden) and Step 4 relation-target verification; fixed description wording to distinguish auto-applied structural fixes from confirm-first content changes.

title: Add consumed-key enforcement for BUILTIN_MENTION_EXCEPTIONS allowlist
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

validate-plugin.mjs's BUILTIN_MENTION_EXCEPTIONS allowlist (keyed "<path>:<Tool>") has no check that a listed exception was ever actually matched during a scan — an entry can go stale (file renamed, mention removed) with nothing flagging it as dead. A type-design-analyzer gate review (Wave 2, SWARM-35) flagged this alongside the sibling KNOWN_BUILTIN_TOOLS staleness gap (that one is now doc-noted in .claude/rules/scripts-and-validation.md as manually maintained; this one is a real ~10-line feature, not a doc note).

- [ ] Track which BUILTIN_MENTION_EXCEPTIONS keys were matched during a scan run
- [ ] Warn (or error) on any allowlist key never matched
- [ ] Add a fixture proving both the "used" and "stale" cases
close_reason: Added consumed-key tracking for BUILTIN_MENTION_EXCEPTIONS: a module-level consumedBuiltinMentionExceptions Set is populated by auditToolReferences() whenever an allowlist .has() check hits, explicitly .clear()-ed right before the real skill-scan loop to wipe self-test pollution (the module-load self-tests exercise the real allowlisted key), then compared post-scan via a new pure findStaleExceptions() helper — unmatched keys get a warn(), not error(), per the staleness-class severity convention. Fixture proves both used-key (silent) and stale-key (warned) cases with synthetic sets; also verified end-to-end by temporarily injecting a bogus allowlist entry and confirming the real scan warns on it while the real Glob entry stays silent (still consumed).

title: Add CI-visible surface for validate-plugin.mjs warn()-level findings
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

validate-plugin.mjs's warn()-level findings (e.g. auditToolReferences's bare-tool-name check) currently only surface as plain-text scrollback in local/CI runs — no GitHub Actions annotation, no PR-visible signal, no warning-count ratchet. A silent-failure-hunter gate review (Wave 2, SWARM-35) flagged this as a real architectural gap: warnings can silently accumulate forever with no CI-visible surface forcing triage.

This is pre-existing and repo-wide (affects every warn() call in validate-plugin.mjs, not something introduced by Wave 2) — needs its own design decision on the right mechanism (GH Actions ::warning:: annotations, a warning-count ratchet failing above a threshold, or something else), not a mechanical fold-in fix.

- [ ] Decide the mechanism (GH annotations vs ratchet vs other)
- [ ] Implement for at least the bare-tool-name warn() path
- [ ] Document the pattern in .claude/rules/scripts-and-validation.md for future warn() additions
close_reason: Added GITHUB_ACTIONS-gated ::warning file=<path>::<message> annotation emission for all 5 warn() call sites in validate-plugin.mjs (properly escaped per GitHub workflow-command rules), plain console.warn output unchanged; documented the pattern in .claude/rules/scripts-and-validation.md; ci.yml needed no change since npm run check's stdout is unredirected.

title: knowledge-maintainer.md: Rule 3 prose uses Edit tool but tools: frontmatter omits it
description:
## Summary

the matching change." The agent's `tools:` frontmatter list is `Read, Glob,
Skill` plus `mcp__basic-memory__*` entries — no `Edit` (and no `Write`/`Bash`
either, so the agent currently has no local-filesystem write capability at
all). Surfaced by the new bare-built-in-tool audit added in vp-claude-98b6
(validate-plugin.mjs `findUndeclaredBuiltinTools`), which reports it as a
warning (not a hard error, since the check is a heuristic — see
scripts-and-validation.md).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `npm run check:plugin`.
2. Observe: `agents/knowledge-maintainer.md: Built-in tool "Edit" referenced
   in prose but missing from tools`.

## Acceptance Criteria
