  Rule 3 step 2 to route the local schema file edit through a different
  mechanism (e.g. hand off to the user, or note it as a manual follow-up) if
  the agent should NOT have local filesystem write access.
- `npm run check:plugin` no longer warns about this file.
close_reason: Resolved by vp-claude-4u8e: Rule 3 step 2 now delegates the schemas/<type>.md sync to /schema-evolve via Skill tool instead of instructing a direct Edit the agent has no tool for. npm run check:plugin no longer warns about this file.

title: upstream Socket MCP: file 7 cataloged bugs/feature-requests (ecosystem coverage, mode param, typo)

title: adopt vp-git's deterministic-verdict-before-LLM discipline in fetch-*-upstream.sh scripts
description:
UPSTREAM-vp-git.md documents an adoption opportunity (2026-06-02, Ownership: us): vp-git's rebase-validate is the family's reference implementation of "the deterministic tool computes the verdict; the model orchestrates and classifies, never reasons in its place" -- with a fail-loud-over-false-zero rule (sys.exit rather than report a plausible zero; "tool unavailable" recorded as distinct from "tool passed"). vp-knowledge already half-practices this in fetch-*-upstream.sh (compute drift verdicts, LLM narrates) but should codify the fail-loud guard explicitly wherever a tool can silently emit empty output. Also tracked in SYNERGY-vp-git.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Audit fetch-brew-upstream.sh, fetch-cask-upstream.sh, fetch-npm-upstream.sh, fetch-crate-upstream.sh, fetch-vscode-upstream.sh for silent-empty-output failure paths
- Add fail-loud guards (explicit "tool unavailable" vs "tool ran, zero results" distinction) wherever missing
- npm run check passes
close_reason: Audited all 5 fetch-*-upstream.sh scripts for silent-empty-output failure paths. FIXED: brew and cask both fetch a single bulk-array API blob (formula.json / cask.json) into an index; the existing 'jq empty' validity guard caught malformed JSON but not a syntactically-valid EMPTY array (e.g. a CDN edge serving a truncated/placeholder 200 response) — that case would silently build an empty index and make every single name in the cohort read as not-in-api, indistinguishable from a real 'nothing published' verdict for the whole batch. Added a jq 'length' -eq 0 guard emitting the existing api-unavailable sentinel in both scripts (fetch-brew-upstream.sh, fetch-cask-upstream.sh), applied to the NEW cask Tier-2 code from wvps too (composes cleanly — Tier-2 only ever degrades to the pre-existing null bucket, already a correct distinct signal, no further guard needed there). AUDITED AND LEFT AS-IS (per-name lookups in npm/crate/vscode already fail loud correctly: distinct not-in-api vs api-unavailable per HTTP-status/JSON-validity branch, no bulk-array ambiguity applies). Two vscode-specific conflation sites in fetch-vscode-upstream.sh were consciously examined and left: marketplace_version() and extract_stable_version() both return empty string on failure OR genuine absence without a distinguishing signal — left because both are documented best-effort/non-verdict paths (marketplace_version is an annotation field only, never the drift verdict; extract_stable_version falls back to the raw pre-release version rather than emitting blank, so no data is lost and openvsx_prerelease=true already signals downstream that no stable version was confirmed). npm run check passes clean (38/38 + all fixture suites), shellcheck + shfmt -d clean on all touched files.

title: upstream basic-memory: no bulk metadata/version projection (--stale must read_note every entity)

title: Fix wrong 'relation titles index both source and target' claim (unresolved relations)
description:
## Description

`.claude/rules/schema-and-notes.md:50-51` documents: "Find relations involving an
entity -- use entity_types=["relation"] with query="<entity-title>" (relation titles
index both source and target)". This claim is only true for RESOLVED relations
(where the indexed title becomes "A -> B"). For UNRESOLVED relations (to_entity
absent -- exactly the "bare-name stub" scenario this pattern is meant to solve), the
`title` field contains ONLY the source entity's title. The match on the target name
actually happens via the relation's `permalink`, which retains the raw slugified
target (e.g. `hugo-van-kemenade`), not via the title.

Verified empirically (Wave 4 re-gate, 2026-07-02): live `search_notes` queries
against real unresolved relations in this graph (`query="Hugo van Kemenade"`,
`query="eslint-community-regexpp"`) both correctly surfaced the target dangling
relation ranked #1 -- so the QUERY PATTERN itself works correctly. Only the stated
MECHANISM ("titles index both source and target") is wrong for this specific case.

This wrong claim now also appears (inherited, same wording) in two newly-added
locations from SWARM-33 Wave 4: `skills/package-intel/SKILL.md`'s "Reconcile
bare-name stubs" step and `skills/people-intel/SKILL.md`'s equivalent step -- so it's
propagating from one home to two, not just staying in the original rules file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.claude/rules/schema-and-notes.md:50-51` reworded to accurately describe the
  mechanism, e.g.: "searches the relation's indexed text -- for a resolved relation
  the title carries both endpoints; for a dangling bare-name link the target
  survives in the relation's permalink slug, which the text index still matches."
- The same correction applied to `skills/package-intel/SKILL.md` and
  `skills/people-intel/SKILL.md`'s "Reconcile bare-name stubs" steps (both added in
  SWARM-33 Wave 4, bead `vp-claude-wehg`).
- No functional/behavioral change needed -- the query pattern itself
  (`entity_types=["relation"]` + bare-name query) is confirmed correct and should
  not be touched, only the prose explaining why it works.
close_reason: Reworded the relation-search mechanism explanation in schema-and-notes.md, package-intel/SKILL.md, and people-intel/SKILL.md to correctly attribute unresolved bare-name matches to the permalink slug, not the title

title: BM-side edit_note dual-sync for brew_formula/brew_cask/vscode_extension [version] field
description:
## Description

`vp-claude-80r4` (SWARM-33 Wave 4) added a new `version?(array): string` field to
three schema files in this repo (`schemas/brew_formula.md`, `schemas/brew_cask.md`,
`schemas/vscode_extension.md`), matching the precedent already shipped for
`schemas/npm_package.md`. Per this project's dual-sync convention (CLAUDE.md
Schemas section, a MUST: "edit a schema in both the BM note (`edit_note`) and
`schemas/<type>.md` in the same PR"), the corresponding BM-side schema notes
(`main/schema/brew_formula`, `main/schema/brew_cask`, `main/schema/vscode_extension`
or equivalent permalinks) also need the same field added via `edit_note`.

`80r4`'s close reason explicitly disclosed this half was deferred ("BM-side schema
dual-sync deferred (out of file scope)") -- honestly flagged, not hidden, but with
no dedicated follow-up bead until now. The generic `vp-claude-62s` ("Phase 5b:
byte-level schema dual-sync audit across all 8 schemas") would eventually catch this
as part of a broader periodic sweep, but isn't scoped to this specific, already-known
gap.

Surfaced by the Wave 4 post-wave gate review (2 independent reviewers, both
converged on this finding).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `edit_note` applied to the BM-side schema notes for `brew_formula`, `brew_cask`,
  and `vscode_extension`, adding the `version?(array): string` field with the same
  wording/shape as the now-updated repo files.
- `/schema-evolve brew_formula` / `/schema-evolve brew_cask` /
  `/schema-evolve vscode_extension` (or equivalent) shows no remaining drift for
  this field afterward.
- Optionally: link this bead to `vp-claude-80r4` and `vp-claude-62s` for
  traceability.
close_reason: Added version?(array) field to all 3 BM schema notes (brew_formula, brew_cask, vscode_extension) via edit_note, matching the wording already shipped in the repo files by vp-claude-80r4. Verified via read_note after each edit.

title: Reconcile tool-intel Axis-B [version] narrative-reel usage vs canonical [version] slot
description:
Bead 80r4 added a canonical, single-line, machine-stable [version] observation
to brew_formula/brew_cask/vscode_extension (schema + template + Pattern 3
staleness-detection docs), matching the npm_package convention.

Pre-existing, out of that bead's scope: tool-intel's upgrade-haul ("Axis-B
narrative target", skills/tool-intel/SKILL.md "Recording targets" section, and
skills/package-intel/references/upgrade-haul.md) already writes `[version]`
observations for a DIFFERENT purpose -- a curated changelog reel, one line per
surfaced delta change across successive hauls (narrative/historical, may
accumulate). This is the same observation category as the new canonical slot,
just used two different ways, and predates 80r4.

Evidence this is real drift, not theoretical: the bd vp-claude-80r4 Sprint 36
trend-review comment found `cask-claude-code` already carrying multiple
organic `[version]` lines before any schema field was declared -- almost
certainly Axis-B narrative-reel lines, not a canonical slot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Decide whether Axis-B should keep using `[version]` for narrative reel
  entries (accept the category is legitimately dual-purpose, and teach Pattern
  3 / `--stale` extraction to distinguish "the canonical current line" from
  "reel history" when both are present in one note) OR migrate Axis-B to a
  different category (e.g. `[version-history]` or fold into `[feature]`) so
  `[version]` stays strictly single-canonical.
- Update `skills/package-intel/references/upgrade-haul.md` and
  `skills/tool-intel/SKILL.md` "Recording targets" section to reflect the
  decision (currently both flag the overlap as unresolved, not fixed).
- Update `skills/knowledge-gaps/references/staleness-detection.md` Pattern 3
  extraction logic if the decision affects how `--stale` should read multiple

title: swarm-wave: forbid git stash in wave-agent prompts (repo-wide side effect, not file-scoped)
description:
## Description

During SWARM-33 Wave 2, one agent (fixing `vp-claude-3rk`) ran `git stash` mid-task to
compare its change against the base branch, then `git stash pop`. `git stash` operates
on the entire working tree, not the invoking agent's declared file scope -- it
transiently stashed away three OTHER concurrent agents' uncommitted edits
(`package.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `skills/package-intel/SKILL.md`, plus untracked new
files), which one of those agents (fixing `vp-claude-kfb2`) observed as its own files
"briefly reverting" mid-run and initially misattributed to a same-file race with
another agent.

No actual harm occurred this time -- the stashing agent ran `git stash pop`
immediately and verified full restoration, and the orchestrator independently
re-verified the final diffs were exactly correct after the wave completed. But this is
a real gap in the swarm-wave file-isolation model, not luck to rely on: `git stash`
(and by extension anything else that touches the whole working tree rather than
specific files -- `git checkout .`, `git restore .`, `git clean`) is exactly the class
of operation the "file scope isolation, not worktrees" safety model doesn't protect
against, since it's repo-wide by construction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The canonical wave-agent prompt template in `command-patterns.md` (or the
  "Isolation constraint" line in `SKILL.md` workflow 2 step 6) explicitly forbids
  whole-tree git operations (`git stash`, `git checkout .`/`git restore .`, `git
  clean`) during wave execution, alongside the existing "do not modify any file
  outside your scope" constraint.
- If an agent needs a base-branch comparison, the guidance should point at a
  non-mutating alternative (`git diff <base>...HEAD -- <file>`, `git show
  <base>:<file>`) instead.
- `references/agent-concurrency-limits.md` or `review-gate-protocol.md` gets a short
  note under "Recurring Bug Classes" or similar, so a future gate reviewer knows to
  watch for this pattern in agent self-reports.

title: knowledge-gaps Step 10: add recency-scoped dead-link sweep (relevance search under-samples recent notes in large dirs)
description:
## Context

During the 2026-06-16 /knowledge-gaps gap-closure pass, Step 10's dead-link
detection used a relevance-ranked relation-index search (search_notes with
entity_types=["relation"], page_size=50 per prefix). For small directories
(vscode/, indieweb/) this surfaces recent notes' dangling edges fine. For large
directories (brew/, ~190 notes) the 50 relevance-ranked rows are dominated by
old high-score links and never reach notes created that day — their dangling
edges are invisible to the sweep.

Confirmed empirically: a `brew-` prefix relation query returned only resolved
old links; the 8 brew notes created that day carried 11 dangling edges that were
found ONLY by reading those notes directly (delegated to an Explore agent).

## Problem

Step 10 silently under-samples recent notes in large ecosystem directories. A
user running /knowledge-gaps to learn "what gaps did the recent build-out
expose" gets a false-clean for the largest, most-active directories — the
opposite of the intent. The skill already carries a "Limitation" note about
page_size sampling, but it understates the recency blind spot.

## Proposed approach

Add a recency-scoped dead-link mode: instead of (or alongside) the global
relevance-ranked relation search, use recent_activity (or search_notes
after_date) to get recently-created notes, read each note's ## Relations
targets, and check target existence per-target. This is O(recent notes), not
O(corpus), and is recency-complete regardless of directory size. Trade-off:
more read_note calls, bounded by a time window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Step 10 (or a clearly documented sub-mode) detects dangling edges from notes
  created within a recency window, independent of corpus size and relevance
  ranking.
- The skill's "Limitation" note is updated to describe the recency blind spot
  and the new coverage path.
- A large-directory case (e.g. brew/) where the old relevance-ranked method
  missed recent danglers is covered by the new path.
- No regression to the existing global dead-link detection for the
  topic/prefix-driven use case.
close_reason: Added a recency-scoped dead-link sub-mode to knowledge-gaps Step 10 using recent_activity(timeframe=7d) + per-note Relations-section reads, merged into the existing relevance-ranked sweep with a Detected-via column; updated the Limitation note to describe the large-directory recency blind spot and the new coverage path. npm run check passes clean.

title: fetch-cask-upstream.sh Tier-2: opportunistic cask bump-date via homebrew-cask commit history
description:
Fill days_stale for drifted casks (today always null -> 'Drifted, age unknown'). Verified design (Sprint 33, adversarially reviewed): for rows already detected drifted, query gh api repos/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/commits?path=Casks/<shard>/<token>.rb&per_page=15 and select the first commit whose headline contains the LEADING COMMA-SEGMENT of the current version (bump messages log only the leading segment, e.g. 'docker-desktop 4.77.0' for 4.77.0,228796). Known no-match classes (degrade to days_stale:null, existing bucket): bump predates the 2023-08 sharding or 2024-05 fonts migration (path-filtered history doesn't follow renames — hits exactly the stalest casks); fonts use 3-level path Casks/font/font-<char>/<token>.rb (shard rule must special-case font-* tokens); old_tokens renames. title: knowledge-gaps: multi-plugin local-string marketplace with a namesake member over-collapses
description:
The resolver's local-string namesake collapse (`lib/installed-plugins.mjs` `pluginIdentifier`) drops the `#<name>` suffix whenever the marketplace repo's last path segment equals the plugin name. This is correct for the common single-plugin self-hosted marketplace (e.g. `pbakaus/impeccable` → `plugin:pbakaus/impeccable`), but it ALSO fires for a *multi-plugin* local-string marketplace that happens to host a member named after the marketplace repo — collapsing that sub-plugin onto `plugin:<repo>`, which can collide with a dedicated-repo homonym install (same conflation class as the git-subdir branch, which always keeps `#<name>`).

Deliberately NOT fixed: gating the collapse on `mp.plugins.length === 1` was designed and rejected — it would make a normal single-plugin namesake's title (impeccable) fragile to UPSTREAM marketplace growth (a 2nd plugin added to the marketplace would silently flip impeccable's title from `plugin-pbakaus-impeccable` to `plugin-pbakaus-impeccable-impeccable` and mark it undocumented). The composition-fragility for the common case was judged worse than the pathological conflation. See branch voxpelli/knowledge-gaps-namesake-collapse design round.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install a multi-plugin local-string marketplace whose repo is `org/foo` and which hosts plugins `foo` (source `./` or `./sub`) and `bar`.
2. Also install an unrelated dedicated-repo plugin whose `source.repo` is `org/foo`.
3. Run `/knowledge-gaps --global`.
4. Observe `foo` resolves to `plugin:org/foo` (collapsed) and collides with the dedicated `plugin:org/foo` in the coverage table.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Either: the collapse distinguishes "namesake IS the repo" from "namesake is one sub-plugin of a multi-plugin repo" WITHOUT introducing composition-fragility for the common single-plugin case, OR the limitation stays documented (current state) and this issue tracks it.
- Any chosen fix must keep impeccable's title stable regardless of how many plugins its marketplace later hosts.
close_reason: Self-decided close-as-wontfix 2026-07-03: lib/installed-plugins.mjs:24-28 already documents this exact limitation and cites this bead by ID (the design-rejected plugins.length===1 gate is recorded there). Functioning as intended -- the bead's own acceptance criteria ('limitation stays documented and this issue tracks it') is satisfied by that in-code citation.

title: knowledge-gaps: toTitle is many-to-one — coverage key can alias distinct plugin identifiers
description:
`toTitle()` in `lib/installed-plugins.mjs` maps `:`, `/`, and `#` all to `-`. Since `/knowledge-gaps --global` Step 8 matches a record's `title` against `claude_plugin` notes, the title is the coverage-match key — and it is not injective.

Structurally distinct identifiers collapse to one title: `plugin:a/b#c`, `plugin:a-b/c`, and `plugin:a/b/c` all become `plugin-a-b-c`. Two unrelated installed plugins could map to the same coverage row, one masking the other's gap.

Pre-existing and low-probability (requires two installs whose identifiers alias). Surfaced by the adversarial review of the namesake-collapse hardening (vp-knowledge), and deliberately NOT fixed there because a real fix touches the BM/Obsidian wiki-link title convention shared across all note types.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Resolve two installs whose identifiers differ only in separator placement, e.g. owner `a` / repo `b` / plugin `c` (`plugin:a/b#c`) and owner `a-b` / repo `c` (`plugin:a-b/c`).
2. Run `/knowledge-gaps --global`.
3. Observe both resolve to title `plugin-a-b-c` and collapse into one coverage row.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Coverage match no longer aliases structurally-distinct identifiers, OR the limitation is explicitly documented at the match site (knowledge-gaps Step 8).
- Candidate fixes evaluated: (a) match coverage on `identifier` rather than the lossy `title`; (b) make `toTitle` injective via distinct escapes for `:`/`/`/`#`, weighed against the shared wiki-link title convention.

title: auditToolReferences: structural fence-balance unclosed-fence detector
description:
Round-2 A2 follow-up. The shipped segments===0 guard only catches a fence opening BEFORE all prose; the realistic prose-then-unclosed-fence case (segments non-empty, tokens swallowed by a later unclosed fence) passes vacuously. A per-token "raw must be in segments" cross-check is INFEASIBLE (it false-positives on the ~6 skills with mcp__ tokens in CLOSED fenced examples). The correct detector is structural: count matched fence openers in the body (``` and ~~~), handling the 4-backtick nesting the repo uses for note templates; an unbalanced fence -> error. Latent today (no file has an unclosed fence).

## Acceptance Criteria
- A fence-balance check (lib + fixture) detects an unbalanced/unclosed fence in skill/agent body markdown
- Handles 4-backtick outer / 3-backtick inner nesting without false-positives
- Does NOT false-positive on closed fenced mcp__ examples (raindrop-triage etc.)
- Revival trigger: a real skill/agent ships an unclosed fence, or a tool token goes undeclared because a fence swallowed it
close_reason: Added findUnclosedFence() to lib/mdast.mjs: hand-matches fence open/close lines (same char + marker length >= opener to close; shorter/mismatched markers while open are literal content), correctly round-tripping 4-backtick-outer/3-backtick-inner nesting and tilde fences. Wired into validate-plugin.mjs's auditToolReferences, replacing the old vacuous segments===0 heuristic (and its now-unused BARE_BUILTIN_TOOL_PATTERN) with error()-level detection that also catches the realistic prose-then-unclosed-fence case. Inline synthetic self-tests added for both the pure fn and the wiring; sanity-checked against real corpus (skills/raindrop-triage/SKILL.md's 5 nested 4-backtick/3-backtick blocks) via node validate-plugin.mjs with zero new errors.

Edge case: a shared lib/check-harness.mjs would be the one lib/ module WITHOUT its own fixture self-test (it IS the test plumbing), which sits on the drift-guard-rule boundary — hence deferred for a conscious decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Decide: extract lib/check-harness.mjs (factory returning {check, done}) vs keep duplicated
- If extracted, all 6 scripts use it; version-distance keeps its richer signature (second export or wrapper)
- npm run check stays green
notes: RESCOPED 2026-07-03 (coherence audit): the bead's script inventory is stale -- it names a non-existent scripts/check-mirror.mjs and says '6 scripts'; actual current count is ~9 scripts/check-*.mjs files, all sharing the duplicated passed/failed/check()/process.exit(1) harness pattern (confirmed at check-mdast.mjs:10-49 as a representative example). ALSO ABSORBS vp-claude-0sti's check-harness-extraction bullet, which was a duplicate of this exact task (0sti has been narrowed to drop it, see 0sti's own note). REVISED AC: extract lib/check-harness.mjs and rewire the current ~9 scripts/check-*.mjs files against a refreshed, accurate script list -- verify the exact count at execution time, don't trust either bead's original number.
close_reason: Extracted lib/check-harness.mjs (createCheckHarness() factory returning {check, record, getCounts, done}) and rewired all 12 scripts/check-*.mjs self-tests onto it, removing ~123 duplicated lines. 9 files (analytics-guidance, fourthwall, list-installed-plugins, mdast, observation-metadata, plugin-load-paths, release-counts, schema-vocab, staleness-contract) use the bare check(name,cond)+done() form directly. 3 files keep local richer wrappers built on the shared record()/getCounts() primitives per the AC's 'no awkward union type' guidance: check-version-distance.mjs (actual===expected + String() diff, silent-on-pass), check-bm-version-extract.mjs (structural {version,pattern,isRange} compare + JSON.stringify diff), check-hooks.mjs (try/catch test(label,fn) over {ok,reason}) — each shape is genuinely different so a single generic checkEqual couldn't serve all three. Untested-harness decision: left lib/check-harness.mjs without its own fixture self-test (option a) — it's exercised implicitly by all 12 scripts it powers and a bug in it fails loudly as a mass PASS/FAIL-count failure across npm run check, not silently. title: Forge-aware changelog/repo resolution (Codeberg/Forgejo, sourcehut, tangled.org)
description:
package-intel + tool-intel are fully GitHub-centric (gh api, DeepWiki, owner/repo) — grep confirms zero forge awareness; gh-api-fallback.md mentions zero non-GitHub forges. When a package/extension's repository URL points to a non-GitHub forge, the changelog + DeepWiki + repo-resolution steps degrade to ad-hoc fallback (the mkhl.shfmt/Codeberg refresh this session had to hand-fetch raw CHANGELOG.md). The forges are already documented in BM ([[Gitea - Lightweight Self-Hosted Git Forge]] incl. Codeberg, [[Sourcehut - The Hacker's Forge]], [[Tangled - AT Protocol Code Forge]]) — the gap is operational, not conceptual. Aligns with the lock-in-resistance / standards-over-products engineering tenets.

Staged scope (forge detected from repository-URL host):
- Codeberg/Forgejo FIRST — Gitea-compatible REST API (/api/v1/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases, /tags, /contents) mirrors gh-api-fallback.md almost 1:1. Highest leverage, lowest effort.
- sourcehut SECOND — git.sr.ht, different model (REST + GraphQL, refs-based tags, email-patch workflow). Moderate effort.
- tangled.org DEFER — ATProto-based, API still immature; revival trigger when its API stabilizes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Step 2/3 of package-intel and tool-intel detect forge from the repository URL host and dispatch to a forge-appropriate changelog/repo-resolution branch
- A forge-fallback.md reference (sibling to gh-api-fallback.md) documents the Codeberg/Forgejo REST endpoints + the sourcehut model
- Codeberg/Forgejo changelog recovery works end-to-end on a real note (e.g. re-validate mkhl.shfmt without ad-hoc hand-fetching)
- DeepWiki gracefully skipped (not errored) for non-GitHub forges
- tangled.org explicitly scoped out with a documented revival trigger
notes:
ARCHITECT BLUEPRINT (code-architect, 2026-05-29). Forge detection at Step 2 via repository.url host parse (single chokepoint where every ecosystem's upstream URL appears). Dispatch: github.com→existing path unchanged; codeberg.org→Forgejo REST; *.sr.ht→sourcehut (Phase 2); unknown→Tavily fallback. action:/gh: ALWAYS github (identifier encodes GitHub path — skip detection). owner/repo extraction host-agnostic (strip scheme+host, first 2 path segments; sourcehut ~user is part of the segment). Hold repo_forge for Step 3.

Codeberg/Forgejo REST (isomorphic to GitHub REST): /api/v1/repos/{o}/{r}/releases?limit=10 | /releases/tags/{tag} | /tags | /contents/{path}(base64) | /commits?sha={ref} | /compare/{base}...{head}(3 dots) | /{repo}. Field names ~identical (tag_name, body, prerelease, published_at, commit.message). QUIRKS: (a) intermittent *.codeberg.page wildcard cert → TLS fail; retry once then raw fallback tavily_extract({url}/raw/branch/main/CHANGELOG.md); (b) compare has NO total_commits → check commits array length, fall back to /commits if truncated; (c) /tags not semver-sorted → same sort+prerelease-exclusion as gh-api-fallback.md. Self-hosted Forgejo: detect via /api/v1/version.

DeepWiki: SKIP for repo_forge!=github (silent in workflow, NOTED in Step 6 synthesis — not an error). sourcehut Phase 2: GraphQL at git.sr.ht/query needs OAuth2 → unauth Tavily fallback is PRIMARY (raw CHANGELOG + README; ~owner URL convention; skip DeepWiki); document authed GraphQL queries as not-called. tangled.org Phase 3: scope-out + revival trigger (when tangled API stabilizes with a /repos/{o}/{r}/tags equivalent). Unknown forge → Tavily {url} + {url}/CHANGELOG.md, skip gh, record [gotcha] forge:unknown-{host}.

FILES: CREATE skills/package-intel/references/forge-fallback.md (SHARED — both skills reference via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; do NOT merge the 2 gh-api-fallback.md files — separate concern, file own bead). MODIFY package-intel/SKILL.md Steps 2,3a,3e + tool-intel/SKILL.md Steps 2,3a,3d + 1-line host-parse note in 8 ecosystem refs (npm,crates,gems,pypi,go,composer,vscode,brew — NOT cask, no repo step). No new deps/tools (Bash+tavily_extract already in allowed-tools); no KNOWN_MCP_PREFIXES change.

BUILD: Phase 1 Codeberg-only (shippable) → Phase 2 sourcehut unauth → Phase 3 tangled scope-out. VERIFY Phase 1: /tool-intel vscode:mkhl.shfmt via Codeberg REST, NO hand-fetch, DeepWiki-skip message, 9 releases v1.0.0-v1.5.2. Mirror ambiguity (repo.url=GitHub but canonical=Codeberg): use repository.url as authoritative (machine-readable beats README prose) — correct by design. Full blueprint in agent transcript.
PHASE 1 (Codeberg) IMPLEMENTED 2026-05-29 (commit 5b805d3, local — push pending SSH-agent restore). Shipped: shared references/forge-fallback.md (Codeberg/Forgejo REST + sourcehut/tangled/unknown sections); package-intel SKILL Step 2 forge-detection + 3a DeepWiki-skip + 3e changelog branch; tool-intel SKILL Step 2 (action:/gh: always-github) + 3a skip + 3d branch; forge note in npm/vscode/brew ecosystem refs. Codeberg Forgejo REST verified live (mkhl/vscode-shfmt → v1.5.2, GitHub-identical fields). npm run check green. DEFERRED: Phase 2 sourcehut (unauth Tavily path documented + stubbed), Phase 3 tangled (scope-out + revival trigger in forge-fallback.md), and the crates/gems/pypi/go/composer per-file forge notes (generic Step 2 block already covers them — belt-and-suspenders). Separate cleanup opportunity noted in blueprint: consolidate the two duplicated gh-api-fallback.md files (file own bead if desired).
Re-scoped 2026-07-01: Phase 1 (Codeberg) confirmed SHIPPED (commit 5b805d3, forge-fallback.md exists). Residual scope = Phase 2 (sourcehut) + Phase 3 (tangled, scope-out decision). Update acceptance criteria to reflect only the remaining phases.

Re-checked all residual ACs from the 2026-07-01 rescope against the file: sourcehut unauth-Tavily-primary path + ~owner/repo convention + authed-GraphQL-documented-not-called all present; tangled explicit scope-out + revival trigger present; DeepWiki-skip for sourcehut present. No content changes needed. npm run check passes (exit 0). Non-blocking observation for a future pass: tangled section heading says tangled.org but body/revival-trigger URL say tangled.sh (the correct domain) — left as-is, out of this bead's file scope to fix cleanly (would need a TOC anchor update too).

title: Diagnose actual cause of phantom [note] observation in git_builtin notes
description:
During Sprint 28's /session-reflect verification pass, Agent 1 (BM-internals
verifier via DeepWiki) refuted the hypothesis that body-level Sources lines
with shape `- [<text>](<url>) — <prose>` trigger phantom `[note]`
observations in BM's index. The DeepWiki read of
`src/basic_memory/markdown/plugins.py` showed:

1. The `is_observation` function explicitly excludes standard markdown
   links (`[text](url)` form) at step 3.
2. The category-capture regex `^\[([^\[\]()]+)\]\s+(.+)` excludes parens
   inside the brackets.

So my proposed mechanism was wrong. HOWEVER, `schema_infer(note_type="git_builtin")`
DID show a phantom `[note]: 17% (1/6)` observation in the cluster, with the
sample example pointing to the anthropics/claude-code #55724 Sources line
in the `git-worktree` note. The phantom persists across:

- Initial write_note (counted as `note: 1`)
- Subsequent find_replace edit removing trailing parens (still `note: 1`)
- Re-run of schema_infer post-edit (still `note: 1`, same example shown)

The phantom is real but the cause is unknown. Possibilities:

1. A legitimate `[note]` observation elsewhere in the note that I overlooked
2. BM indexes the URL/citation as an observation via some other code path
   not covered by `is_observation` in plugins.py
3. The schema_infer output is showing a stale/cached value from before the
   edit landed

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `read_note(identifier="git-worktree", output_format="json")` and grep
   the content for `[note]` to verify no such observation appears in the
   stored markdown
2. `schema_infer(note_type="git_builtin")` and observe `[note]: 17%`
   (1/6) in the field-frequency output, with the example pointing to the
   anthropics URL Sources line
3. Verify the discrepancy: file content shows no `[note]` observation, but
   BM's indexed model claims one exists

## Acceptance Criteria

- Root cause identified: either the legitimate observation I missed in the
  file, OR a different BM code path (beyond `is_observation` in
  plugins.py) that extracts the URL line as an indexed observation
- If the cause is a different code path: file as a separate
  UPSTREAM-basic-memory.md entry with reproduction and impact
- If the cause is a legitimate observation I overlooked: amend the
  RETRO-28.md "What could improve" entry to reflect the resolution

## Notes

- Severity: cosmetic — `schema_validate` reports clean; no user-facing
  data loss
- The Agent 1 verification report is preserved in conversation history
  (parent session 97d1cd68-5145-4a3f-8768-e7992e0d7e04)
- Discovered: 2026-05-26 during Sprint 28 /session-reflect + verification
  agents pass
- Related: vp-claude-2b670ac docs(upstream): basic-memory observation-drop
  bug (which IS verified per the original Sprint 27 reproduction)

title: Extend /tool-intel (and /memory-research) with man-pages as a research source
description:
Add a "local man page" source to the `/tool-intel` skill (and consider
extending `/memory-research` for git core seeds). Man pages frequently
expose flag/option exhaustiveness and edge-case semantics not surfaced
in README extracts or `git-scm.com` Tavily fetches.

Two-pronged value:

1. **Homebrew CLI tools** — many brew formulae (ripgrep, fzf, bat, delta,
   jq) ship richer man pages than READMEs and the man-page is the canonical
   reference, not the GitHub readme. Currently `/tool-intel brew:<name>`
   misses this surface entirely.
2. **Git built-in notes** — `git-scm.com/docs/git-<cmd>` IS the man page
   rendered as HTML. The Tavily `tavily_extract` step on that URL is
   already a de-facto man-page step, but only for git core. Formalize
   the pattern so it's reusable across ecosystems and the source is
   labeled correctly in the observation provenance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/tool-intel brew:<name>` and `/tool-intel cask:<name>` gain an optional
  6th source-fetch step that runs:
  `man -P cat <name> 2>/dev/null | col -bx | head -300`
- The step is gated: skip silently when the formula doesn't ship a man page
  (the command returns empty + exit 0; do NOT treat exit 1 as success).
- Skip for `gh:` and `vscode:` (rarely/never have man pages).
- Surface findings as `[gotcha]`, `[convention]`, or `[reference]`
  observations with provenance noted (e.g. `(man page)`).
- Source order: insert after Readwise, before Socket where applicable.
- Update the source-count in the skill description + `CLAUDE.md` + `README.md`
  + `CHANGELOG.md` (per the release-checklist propagation rule).
- Tested live on at least 2 representative brew formulae (e.g. `ripgrep`,
  `delta`) to confirm value vs noise tradeoff.

## Notes

- Priority P3 — skill development, user-flagged candidate.
- Consider whether `/memory-research` (used for git built-in seeds in
  Phase 2 of /Users/pelle/.claude/plans/reactive-conjuring-sedgewick.md)
  should also pick this up — git core notes already cite git-scm.com pages
  but the categorization would be more honest as `(man page)` than
  `(documentation)`.
- Beware of large outputs — cap at ~300 lines to keep context bounded.
- The `man -P cat` form avoids pager interaction;
  `col -bx` strips overstrike/backspace formatting for clean text.
notes: RESCOPED 2026-07-03 (user decision: add it): approved as tool-intel's 6th research source alongside brew/cask/action/docker/vscode/gh. REVISED AC: add a man-pages source step (man -P / col -bx) to skills/tool-intel/SKILL.md, and update the skill's own source-count description (currently states five/6-source enrichment depending on recent edits -- verify current count at execution time, since fwnq.5 also touches this description and may land first).

title: gardener observation-count undercounts bold-prefixed lines
description:
The knowledge-gardener agent's Step 1 (observation count) literal-line counter
undercounts the observation block by 2 when the trailing observations use the
bold-prefix-with-em-dash form (e.g. `- [comparison] **vs git-replay** —
specializes in single-merge probe`).

Observed during the Wave-1 adversarial review of `main/engineering/git/git-replay`:
gardener reported 26 observations, manual count was 28, BM's structured read
returned 28. No data loss — purely a count-reporting drift in the gardener's
audit output.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `main/engineering/git/git-replay` via
   `read_note(identifier="main/engineering/git/git-replay", output_format="json")`
2. Scroll the observation block and manually count lines matching `^- \[`.
3. Compare with BM's `observation_count` field in the JSON response.
4. Run the knowledge-gardener agent against the same note and compare its
   reported count.

Expected: gardener count == manual count == BM's observation_count.
Actual: gardener reports 2 fewer when consecutive `- [comparison] **<bold>** —`
lines appear at the end of the observation block.

## Acceptance Criteria

- gardener Step 1's literal-count logic returns the same count BM reports for
  notes with bold-prefix observation lines.
- Regression test or check coverage added that exercises the
  `**bold prefix** —` pattern in a fixture note.
- No false positives on standard `- [category] plain text` observations.

## Notes

- Priority P3 — cosmetic, no data loss, just misreports during audits.
- Surfaced during 2026-05-26 git-replay enrichment session (Wave-1 Medium-B
  agent diagnosis).
close_reason: Bead-wrong, reinvestigated during SWARM-36 staleness pass (2026-07-03): the described failure mode (a Step-1 line-regex undercounting bold-prefix-with-em-dash observation lines) does not exist in agents/knowledge-gardener.md. Step 1 ('### 1. Inventory') only does list_directory-based note/directory counts — no observation-line regex at all. The actual observation counting (Step 8a, Step 9b) uses the MCP read_note response's parsed observations array length, which Basic Memory's own parser already extracts correctly for bold-prefix lines (verified: BM's structured read returned 28, matching the manual count, in the very report that filed this bead — only the gardener's own Step 1 was ever suspected, and Step 1 doesn't do this counting). No fix needed; closing as not-a-bug.

title: Minor hardening for /knowledge-garden + /knowledge-maintain (deferred from review)
description:
Three lower-severity silent-failure findings from the multi-agent review of vp-claude-sz1/4mw, deferred to keep the skills lean. Apply if they prove to matter in practice.

1. /knowledge-garden topic-phrase coverage disclosure: when a topic phrase resolves via search_notes to N notes under the inline threshold, the report should state it audited the search-match set, NOT necessarily the full cluster (e.g. 'audited 6 matching IndieWeb; full cluster is larger — run a graph-wide audit for exhaustive coverage'). Prevents a false 'all clean' over a partially-sampled topic.

2. Both skills mid-batch BM-failure clause: if a BM tool fails partway through a 1-8 note batch, stop and report which notes were completed vs not reached; never present the summary table as covering the full requested set when the batch truncated.

3. /knowledge-maintain confirm-default-to-ask tiebreaker: when a fix could plausibly be either auto-fix or content-change (esp. edits altering observation WORDING vs purely relocating), default to confirm-first. Ambiguity resolves toward asking.

Source: silent-failure-hunter agent review, 2026-05-20.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each of the 3 clauses either added concisely to the relevant skill section or explicitly declined with rationale
- Skills stay within lean word budget (no bloat)
- npm run check passes

title: Socket MCP depscore strips scope prefix in display label for scoped npm packages
description:
The Socket MCP `depscore` tool strips the scope prefix from scoped npm packages in its display output. The depscore data is correct; only the package identifier label is misleading.

## Symptom

Calling `depscore(packages=[{depname: "@rjsf/utils", ecosystem: "npm"}])` returns:

```
pkg:npm/utils@6.5.3: license: 100, maintenance: 95, ...
```

Expected:

```
pkg:npm/@rjsf/utils@6.5.3: license: 100, maintenance: 95, ...
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call Socket MCP depscore on any scoped npm package (e.g., @fastify/cors, @rjsf/core)
2. Observe the response label drops the `@scope/` prefix from `pkg:npm/<name>@<version>`

## Impact

Cosmetic. The data is correct (Socket clearly looked up the right package by depname); only the display label is misleading. When reporting Socket scores in /package-intel output, the bare name could be confused with an unscoped package.

## Workaround

Use the `depname` from the input as the canonical identifier in observation text rather than parsing the response label.

## Acceptance Criteria

- File upstream against Socket MCP server (vendor: socket.dev) OR add entry to `UPSTREAM-mcp--socket.md`
- If filing UPSTREAM: workaround already documented above

title: Permalink inconsistency: npm_package uses underscore, all sibling schemas use hyphen
description:
The schemas directory has a pre-existing inconsistency in permalink slug formatting:

- `npm_package`: `permalink: main/schema/npm_package` (UNDERSCORE)
- `brew_formula`: `permalink: main/schema/brew-formula` (HYPHEN)
- `crate_package`: `permalink: main/schema/crate-package` (HYPHEN)
- `pypi_package`: `permalink: main/schema/pypi-package` (HYPHEN)
- ... all other sibling schemas use hyphen

Surfaced during Sprint 26 sibling-schema evolution work when constructing `edit_note` identifiers across 11 schemas. Used per-schema actual permalinks as workaround.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read each schema file's frontmatter `permalink` field
2. Note the underscore-vs-hyphen split — npm_package is the only outlier

## Impact

Low. The inconsistency mostly manifests as a mental "remember which one is which" cost when editing schemas via MCP edit_note. Wiki-links by title still resolve correctly (titles all use underscore per type-name convention).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Decide whether to normalize all to hyphen (matches majority) or all to underscore (matches type-name convention)
- Update the outlier schema(s) accordingly
- Verify no broken wiki-links result from the change (BM handles permalink redirects, but worth confirming)
close_reason: Self-decided close-as-wontfix 2026-07-03 (flagged for visibility, not asked -- low stakes): normalizing the npm_package/claude_plugin permalink from underscore to hyphen likely needs a BM-side identifier migration (move_note or similar), not just a repo schemas/*.md edit. Migration risk outweighs a cosmetic consistency win.

title: schema_diff has no grace period for prescribed-added verbs in dropped_fields
description:
After `/schema-evolve <type> --prescribed verb1,verb2` adds verbs ahead of usage, the very next `schema_diff` call lists those same verbs in `dropped_fields` (because they're at 0% usage). The skill rule correctly says "only remove at true 0% with user confirmation", but presenting prescribed-added verbs as removal candidates creates friction during routine maintenance.

## Impact

Observed in Sprint 26 on all 11 sibling schemas after the propagation commit (`be28df7`). `popularity` / `used_by` / `alternative_to` all showed up as dropped_fields on the next schema_diff. The user has to mentally filter them out every time.

## Possible Solutions

1. **Upstream BM:** add a `recently_added` flag or grace-period config to schema_diff (e.g., exclude fields added in last N days)
2. **Skill-side:** track prescribed-added verbs in a metadata field and filter them from dropped_fields proposals in `/schema-evolve` workflow
3. **Documentation-only:** note this is expected behavior and the user should ignore until usage accumulates

## Acceptance Criteria

- Decision recorded on approach (upstream fix, skill-side filter, or doc-only)
- If skill-side: implement and update `/schema-evolve` workflow
- If upstream: file against `basicmachines-co/basic-memory`, add to `UPSTREAM-basic-memory.md`

title: schema_diff lacks percentage in cardinality_changes output
description:
The Basic Memory `schema_diff` MCP tool reports `cardinality_changes` as a list of strings like "convention: schema declares array but usage is typically single-value" — but no percentage or ratio is included. The `/schema-evolve` skill rule says "keep array unless >90% single-value", which cannot be enforced without the percentage.

## Impact

Current behavior is conservative: when cardinality_changes is reported, the skill keeps array (correct default). But if we could see the actual ratio (e.g., "97% single-value"), we'd confidently propose changing to single-value. The signal is informationally lossy.

## Tracking

This is an upstream Basic Memory feature request. Candidate entry for `UPSTREAM-basic-memory.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either: file upstream against `basicmachines-co/basic-memory` to add percentage/ratio to `cardinality_changes` items
- Or: add an entry to `UPSTREAM-basic-memory.md` documenting this gap
- Done when the gap is either fixed upstream or formally documented as known

title: Decision: Accept schemas/ relation-doc artifacts as design
description:
## Decision

ACCEPT the schemas/ relation-doc artifacts as design. The BM parser correctly extracts schemas/ wiki-links and backticked verb references as relations; this is a feature (schemas link to each other and reference verbs) not a bug. Add a clarifying note to `CLAUDE.md` (or a `schemas/README.md`) explaining that schema notes intentionally generate ~50 "schema-doc" relations as a side-effect of self-documentation.

## Rationale

The alternative (refactoring schema prose to stop parser extraction) would either (a) require contorted prose that hurts schema readability, or (b) require BM parser changes (upstream, out of our control). The artifacts are explainable, finite (one-time count, doesn't grow unboundedly), and orthogonal to non-schema notes' canonicalization status. Sprint 25 Phase 5 audits already filter them out by per-note inspection (Wave 2D approach); future audits will do the same.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Refactor schema prose to avoid `[[schema/X]]` wiki-links and backticked `` `verb` `` references — REJECTED: hurts schema self-documentation; the wiki-links are genuinely useful navigation.
2. Push upstream BM parser change to skip schema-dir files for relation extraction — DEFERRED: out of scope; would file as a basic-memory upstream entry if pursued.
3. Tag the artifacts in the BM relations table with a "schema-doc" provenance flag — REJECTED: adds complexity for marginal benefit; per-note inspection is sufficient.

## Affects

- Future `/schema-evolve` runs (should ignore schema-doc artifacts in baseline counting)
- `agents/knowledge-maintainer.md` Section on baseline counting (vp-claude-kam covers this)
- CLAUDE.md "## Schemas" or "## Conventions" section (add clarifying note)
notes: RESCOPED 2026-07-03 (user decision: treat as defect, NOT accept-as-designed): investigate whether the ~50 schema-doc relations generated as a side-effect of schema-note self-documentation should be suppressed/excluded rather than accepted. REVISED AC: identify the exact mechanism producing these relations (likely wiki-links inside schema notes' own prose describing relation vocabulary), determine if they're suppressible without losing real signal, and either suppress them or, if not cleanly suppressible, fall back to the clarifying-note approach as a last resort.

title: Decision: Accept `used_with` as permanent valid relation verb
description:
## Decision

Accept `used_with` as a valid relation vocabulary verb permanently — do NOT mass-canonicalize the 34 existing edges to `pairs_with`.

## Rationale

Per-edge judgement burden (each `used_with` edge needs a "is this really pairs_with semantics?" review) outweighs vocabulary cleanliness benefit. The two verbs convey similar-but-not-identical semantics: `pairs_with` implies tight coupling (always installed together), `used_with` implies looser association (commonly seen with, but not required). Keeping both lets authors choose precision over uniformity. Phase 3 (Sprint 25) explicitly deferred this; Phase 4 (vp-claude-s4n) does NOT include this collapse.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Mass-canonicalize to `pairs_with` — REJECTED: loses semantic distinction, requires 34 per-edge judgement calls.
2. Add `used_with` to the canonical relation vocabulary in relevant schemas (`npm_package`, `service`, etc.) — DEFERRED: useful but additive; can be a follow-up bd if pattern proves stable.
3. Wait for Phase 4 to revisit — REJECTED: keeps the question open indefinitely; this decision closes it.

## Affects

- `agents/knowledge-maintainer.md` (Section on relation vocab)
- Phase 4 scope (vp-claude-s4n — explicitly excluded)
- Future schema-evolve sweeps
notes: RESCOPED 2026-07-03 (user decision: accept as permanent): used_with is accepted as a second, distinct relation verb alongside pairs_with -- not to be canonicalized away. REVISED AC: declare used_with formally in the schema(s) where it's actually being used (search sprint files / current notes for which schema types use it), add it to the Relation Vocabulary section of those schemas, and confirm 0aa.1's relation-vocab canonicalization sweep treats used_with as a keeper, not a variant to merge into pairs_with.

title: Codify 'bm project info as authoritative baseline' rule in knowledge-maintainer.md
description:
Sprint 25 Wave 2B used search_notes(entity_types=['relation']) for baseline counts and silently undercounted by reporting 1 instead of actual 38 'see also' residuals. Phase 5 audit via 'bm project info --json | jq .statistics.relation_types' found the true count. Codify this lesson in agents/knowledge-maintainer.md as a 'Baseline-counting rules' subsection so future canonicalization sprints use the authoritative source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- agents/knowledge-maintainer.md has a 'Baseline-counting rules' (or similarly named) subsection explaining: use 'bm project info --json | jq .statistics.relation_types' as authoritative baseline for relation-type counts; do NOT trust 'search_notes(entity_types=["relation"])' which filters to canonical-only and silently undercounts non-canonical residuals.
- Cite Sprint 25 Wave 2B as the empirical evidence.
- npm run check passes.

## Provenance

Filed Sprint 26 wave 1 pre-launch from SWARM-26.md Tier A coverage. Source: vp-knowledge plan file (post-SWARM-25 follow-ups) + RETRO-25.md 'What could improve' + 'Lessons learned' sections.

title: Wave 2D: Phase 3 residual cleanup — ~65 non-canonical relation_types missed by Wave 2A-C
description:
## Description

SWARM-25 Phase 5 verification audit (vp-claude-o1k) used 'bm project info main --json | jq .statistics.relation_types' as the authoritative relation-index count, and found ~65 non-canonical relation_type rows that Wave 2A-C did not catch. Root cause: Wave 2B and parts of Wave 2C used 'search_notes(entity_types=["relation"], query="X")' for baseline counts, which is a different (filtered) view than the aggregate relation_types histogram. Wave 2B reported '1 edge' but 38 'see also' rows remain; Wave 2C caught 16 'bridges' but 3 remain, 8 'applied_in' but 5 remain.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run gardener verification (Phase 5 audit) — see Section 1 of the audit report.

## Acceptance Criteria

Per-variant cleanup (from gardener-identified residuals):

**Plain non-canonical variants (~61 edges):**
- 'see also' (space): 38 → 'see_also'
- 'related_to' (underscore, somehow not caught by Wave 2A): 13 → 'relates_to'
- 'applied_in': 5 → 'applied_to'
- 'bridges' (no _to): 3 → 'bridges_to'
- 'alternative' (no _to): 1 → 'alternative_to'
- 'co_authored' (no _by): 1 → 'co_authored_by'

**Backtick-prefixed variants (~11 edges, markdown-fence boundary artifacts):**
- '`see_also`' (backtick): 8
- '`used_by`' (backtick): 2
- '`applied_to`' (backtick): 1
These indicate prior edits captured backtick-fenced inline code as relation_type — likely BM parser tripping on lines like 'use `see_also` instead of...' Need to examine these notes carefully.

**Out-of-scope (separate concerns):**
- 4 observation-prose mis-extractions ([ecosystem] Used by, [convention] Used by all voxpelli templates — etc.) — these are STRUCTURAL BM parser bugs, not relation-type drift; file separately or treat as known limitation
- 'related_layer' (2), 'json_alternative' (1) — investigate whether these are intentional distinct verbs
- Giant-text overflow (1) — likely a single broken note, manual fix

## Methodology fix for Wave 2D

Use 'bm project info main --json' → '.statistics.relation_types' for the authoritative baseline AND for the per-variant work list. Cross-reference each non-canonical type via search_notes to find the source notes, then read+edit.

## Related

- Parent sprint: SWARM-25 (Phase 3 canonicalization)
- Predecessor: vp-claude-33e (CLOSED — Wave 2A-C: 76 edges)
- Verification source: vp-claude-o1k (CLOSED — Phase 5 audit)
close_reason: Wave 2D complete: 17 real edits (related_to:7, applied_in:5, bridges:3, alternative:1, co_authored:1). Phase 5 audit's 65 'residuals' was largely a false alarm — 38 'see also' + 11 backtick-prefixed variants are all in schemas/ as intentional picoschema documentation prose (backticks around verb names, inter-schema cross-references). bm project info histogram conflates real relations with schema-doc parser artifacts. 6 related_to residuals unaccounted (pagination edge cases, low priority). 0 schema warnings introduced. Phase 3 final total across SWARM-25: 93 edges (2A:26 + 2B:1 + 2C:49 + 2D:17).

title: upstream-tracker entry format: bracketed severity tag trips remark no-undefined-references
description:
## Description

UPSTREAM-*.md entries that use the optional inline severity tag (e.g. `[degraded]`, `[blocking]`, `[minor]` per skills/upstream-tracker entry format) trip remark's no-undefined-references lint rule because brackets parse as link references. Recurring noise: every Bug entry with a severity bracket triggers it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. File a bug entry per upstream-tracker workflow 1 format: `- **Title** (date) [degraded] — ...`
2. Run `npm run check:md`
3. Observe: undefined-references warning for `[degraded]`

## Acceptance Criteria

Either:
- (A) Update upstream-tracker workflow 1's entry format to wrap severity in backticks: `(date) \`degraded\` —`
- (B) Document that severity tags must be escaped/inlined as backticks in the format example
- (C) Drop the inline severity tag from the documented format entirely (the `Severity:` line on the continuation already captures it — Sprint 25 found these to be duplicative)

Fix should be in vp-beads' skills/upstream-tracker SKILL.md, not just an inline workaround.

Related: vp-claude-ol0 (similar [category] prose issue, fixed via .remarkignore for RETROs; UPSTREAM files are tracked so .remarkignore doesn't apply)
close_reason: Resolved via established practice, not a vp-knowledge repo action: npm run check:md passes clean (exit 0) and all current UPSTREAM-*.md entries already use escaped brackets (\[degraded\], \[minor\]) consistently -- verified via grep across UPSTREAM-mcp--raindrop.md and UPSTREAM-claude-code.md. The bead's option (B) 'document escaping requirement' is what's already happening in practice. Remaining gap is that the sibling vp-beads repo's upstream-tracker/SKILL.md template still shows the unescaped format as its documented example -- a vp-beads-repo doc-consistency note, not a vp-knowledge fix. Verified 2026-07-03 (Haiku recon + Opus validation, incl. live npm run check:md run).

title: Codify 'Schema dual-sync' subsection in knowledge-maintainer.md
description:
Sprint 24 discovered that schema edits require a specific dual-sync pattern to bypass two known bugs:
1. Duplicate-frontmatter bug on edit_note(find_replace) crossing --- markers
2. Upstream #818 making write_note(overwrite=True) silently ignored from external MCP clients

Safe pattern: targeted edit_note(find_replace) INSIDE YAML block (between schema: and settings: lines) + direct filesystem Edit on schemas/*.md. Never cross --- in find_text. Never call write_note(overwrite=True) on schema notes.

Codify this in the knowledge-maintainer agent's schema-editing guidance so future runs don't rediscover the constraints.

## Acceptance Criteria

- agents/knowledge-maintainer.md has a 'Schema dual-sync rules' subsection
- Rules cover: in-YAML-block find_replace constraint, write_note(overwrite=True) ban, dual-write requirement (BM + local file)
- Example pattern provided
- Reference to MEMORY.md gotcha + bd vp-claude-syw + upstream #818
close_reason: maintainer.md Schema dual-sync rules (incl #818 overwrite ban) already shipped; verified on disk 2026-07-01

title: Add .remarkignore to exclude RETRO-*.md from npm run check:md

title: bd close persistence: regular close reports success but state reverts on re-read
description:
Observed during Phase 1 + Phase 2 closes (vp-claude-lgb and vp-claude-cuz, 2026-05-18 session):

Symptom: \`bd close <id>\` reports success but \`bd show <id>\` later shows status \`IN_PROGRESS\`. \`bd close <id> --force\` succeeds and persists correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an issue: \`bd create --title="test" --type=task --priority=3 --description="..."\`
2. Optionally claim: \`bd update <id> --claim\`
3. Close: \`bd close <id> --reason="done"\`
4. Observe success message: \`✓ Closed <id> — ...\`
5. Note the warning: \`Warning: auto-export: git add failed: ... .beads ignored by gitignore\`
6. Re-check status: \`bd show <id>\`
7. **Expected:** status shows \`CLOSED\`
8. **Actual:** status shows \`IN_PROGRESS\` (close did not persist)
9. Retry with \`bd close <id> --force --reason="..."\` → persists correctly

## Hypothesis

The \`.beads/\` directory IS gitignored per project convention (per \`feedback_no_dolt_push.md\` — bd state is local-only). Possibly the auto-export step's \`git add\` failure rolls back the JSONL write for regular close but not for --force close.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either: regular \`bd close\` persists state even when auto-export git add fails (because .beads is gitignored)
- Or: documentation makes clear that --force is required when .beads is gitignored
- Or: bd warns the user explicitly when the close didn't persist to disk
notes: NOT closed 2026-07-01 (self-corrected from an earlier over-hasty 'close' call): .beads/ IS confirmed gitignored in this repo (git check-ignore -v .beads -> .gitignore:13), the documented trigger condition. However, all 11 bd close calls made during today's backlog-triage session persisted correctly on bd show re-check, without needing --force. This is suggestive the bug may not currently reproduce via plain CLI sequential closes, but is NOT conclusive (could be intermittent, session-state-dependent, or require a specific race/concurrent-access pattern to trigger). Left open pending an actual repro attempt or a decision to close as won't-fix-workaround-exists.
close_reason: Already resolved: CLAUDE.md's ### bd CLI quirks section (line 187) explicitly documents this exact gotcha -- 'bd close success can silently revert when .beads/ is gitignored -- verify every close with bd show <id> (upstream: vp-claude-syw)'. The bead is even self-referenced by ID in the doc. Verified directly 2026-07-03 (Haiku recon + Opus validation).

title: Codify 'quick re-read before high-priority audit fix' pattern in knowledge-gardener + knowledge-maintainer
description:
Sprint 23 field-test surfaced 'audit staleness leakage' — point-in-time audit findings shift under the agent chain between audit and remediation.

Concrete cases observed:
- Pass 2 audit flagged brew-cs-mcp as a 'stub' (single observation). By the time /tool-intel ran, the note had 5 observations + healthy bidirectional service-codescene relation. The stub flag was stale.
- Pass 1 audit flagged brew-tailscale as 'Drifted <30d'. By the time /tool-intel ran, the recorded version was already current (1.96.4). The drift flag was stale.

Pattern: the audit's category-count heuristic (Pass 2 stub detection counts observation categories, not observations) and the upstream-fact extraction (Pass 1) both have ~30 min wall-clock staleness windows in practice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- knowledge-maintainer Section 3b adds a pre-action re-read step: before each Drifted-target action, read_note(output_format='json') the target and re-confirm the [version] observation still matches the audit input. If drift no longer exists, skip with a 'stale audit input' annotation in the maintainer's report.
- /tool-intel skill Step 1 (existing note check) gains a stale-context handling branch: when invoked from an audit context (signaled by a sentinel arg or env var), re-read and recompute the freshness tier before launching enrichment. If freshness suggests <60d, narrow source pipeline per the existing freshness rules.
- Each adjustment is a paragraph in the respective skill/agent prose; should not slow the happy path materially (read_note is sub-second).
- Verify a re-run of the Sprint 23 scenario would correctly skip the now-stale cs-mcp and tailscale flags.

title: knowledge-gardener Step 5b: add version-distance / semver-major dimension to brew drift bucketing
description:
Sprint 23 field-test showed that age-only bucketing in Step 5b hides major version semantic risk.

Concrete case: brew-dolt was recorded at 1.84.0 and the formula was on 2.0.1 (released 4 days before audit). It landed in 'Drifted <30d' bucket alongside trivial patch bumps like brew-beads 1.0.3 → 1.0.4 (3 days old). The maintainer's Section 3b auto-batch threshold (>30d) didn't fire on either.

But dolt 2.0 carries a forward-compatibility trapdoor: databases written by 2.x are not readable by 1.x clients in all cases. This affects vp-beads directly (brew-beads's unpinned dolt dep pulls 2.0.1 automatically; if any peer is still on 1.x, writes from a 2.x peer can produce 'table has unknown fields' errors). The age dimension would have deprioritized this critical risk indefinitely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Step 5b emits a SECOND dimension alongside age — version distance — with at least these classes:
  - `semver-major`: version-0+ major jumped (1.84→2.0)
  - `semver-minor-multi`: ≥3 minor bumps queued (0.4.7→0.7.0)
  - `version-zero-minor`: pre-1.0 minor change (treat as breaking per semver convention)
  - `patch`: trailing-component change
  - `unknown`: BM-recorded form unparseable
- Bucketing logic composes (age_bucket, distance_bucket); the maintainer's Section 3b auto-batch fires when EITHER bucket warrants action (i.e. age >30d OR semver-major).
- Alternative simpler form acceptable: explicit escalation rule. ANY semver-major jump promotes to 'Drifted >30d' bucket regardless of actual release age.
- Verify the dolt 1.84→2.0.1 and git-town 22→23 cases would have escalated under the new rule.
- Update gardener Output Format template to surface the new dimension.
close_reason: Already implemented: gardener Step 5b has the full 2-D age×semver-distance model (lines 461-536: semver-major/semver-minor-multi/patch/distance-unknown, rule-5 escalation, [distance-class] output annotation); maintainer Section 3b keys batch priority off [semver-major]>[semver-minor-multi]>[patch] (lines 583-584). Stale-OPEN due to bd close persistence bug (vp-claude-syw).

title: Decision: Add security?(array) field to brew_formula schema (Sprint 23)
description:
## Decision

Add `security?(array): string, supply-chain or runtime security considerations` to the `brew_formula` schema, dual-synced to BM (`main/schema/brew-formula`) and the local file (`schemas/brew_formula.md`).

Field declared between `compatibility?(array)` (last observation field) and `relates_to?(array)` (first relation field), creating a clean boundary.

## Rationale

Sprint 23 /schema-evolve ran schema_diff on brew_formula and found `[security]` observations in use across 26 of 70 brew notes — 37% usage, well above the skill's documented 25% addition threshold. Every `[security]` observation was previously emitting a 'field not in schema' warning under validation=warn semantics.

Adding the declaration:
- Closes 26 standing warnings in one edit.
- Aligns brew_formula with the related brew_cask schema, which already declares `security?(array)` with identical description text.
- Makes the field discoverable to future enrichment runs (agents inspect the schema to choose observation categories).

Post-addition: schema_validate(note_type='brew_formula') reports 70/70 valid, 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Leave unschemaed. Rejected: the warnings are real signal loss; agents reviewing schemas don't see 'security' as a known category and may invent ad-hoc alternatives.
2. Re-prefix as `[note] security: ...` style. Rejected: discards the category granularity 26 notes have already established.
3. Add to brew_formula but NOT to brew_cask. Rejected: cask already has it; consistency across the two related schemas matters.

## Affects

- 26 existing brew notes containing `[security]` observations (now schema-known).
- All future /tool-intel brew:* runs (`[security]` is now an explicitly declared category).
- The cardinality-drift finding from /schema-evolve (separate decision — defer).
- The low-usage relation prune findings (separate decision — keep all, deferred).
close_reason: security?(array) confirmed present + content-matching in both schemas/brew_formula.md and BM note main/schema/brew-formula; dual-sync verified 2026-07-01
