title: Dedup parallel-agent-orchestration-lessons + capture edit_note validation-error gotcha
description:
## The state

The BM note 'engineering/agents/parallel-agent-orchestration-lessons' currently has duplicate observations from a botched session-reflect run on 2026-05-06:

- Pattern 'Argument intent inference for cross-ecosystem skill input' — 2 copies (identical)
- Pattern 'Design guardrails for graceful failure, not self-policing' — 2 copies (one with literal '[[wiki-links]]' in backticks; one rewritten to avoid the literal brackets)
- Lesson 'Discovery cost recurs even when workaround fix cost is low' — 2 copies (identical)
- Pattern 'Treat user Socratic questions as explicit confidence checks' — 2 copies (one with 'wasn't there before'; one with 'was not there before')

Total: 8 lines of duplicate observations.

## The validation-error-doesn't-roll-back finding

Discovered during the same session: edit_note via the BM MCP can return a Pydantic validation error response while STILL applying the find_replace to disk. The 'Edit Failed' response is misleading on this code path — partial application happens despite the error.

Concrete sequence: I ran an edit_note with a Pattern 2 observation containing '[[wiki-links]]' in backticks. The text was actually written to disk, but the parser then read it back and triggered a 200-char relation_type cap error (the parser is markdown-blind on this token; backticks do not escape the bracket marker). The error response made it look like the edit failed, so I retried with the bracket marker rewritten — and the retry's find_text matched the not-actually-rolled-back stored content, so it appended a SECOND copy. Same shape played out for the Socratic-pattern observation.

This is a meaningful BM MCP behavior gotcha worth documenting alongside the related parser-cap and graceful-failure patterns.

## Cleanup procedure

This is the canonical 'observation duplication on an existing BM note' workflow that bd vp-claude-2yk was filed to bridge. While that bug is unresolved, the cleanup must run via main-session write_note(overwrite=true):

1. Read the full note via read_note (multi-page; ~50KB)
2. Construct a deduplicated version locally — remove the 4 duplicate observations
3. Append a NEW [gotcha] observation capturing the validation-error-doesn't-roll-back finding
4. Write back via write_note(overwrite=true)
5. Verify via search_notes for each kept observation's unique phrase

## Acceptance criteria

- The note 'engineering/agents/parallel-agent-orchestration-lessons' has exactly ONE copy of each of the 4 observations involved in the incident
- A new [gotcha] observation captures the rule: 'edit_note validation errors do not guarantee rollback — content may be applied to disk despite error response. Always verify with read_note before retrying.'
- search_notes for each unique phrase returns exactly one match in the note

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read parallel-agent-orchestration-lessons via the BM MCP filesystem (~/basic-memory/engineering/agents/Parallel Agent Orchestration Lessons.md is the disk path; ALWAYS use mcp__basic-memory__read_note in normal work, this path is for diagnosis only)
2. grep -n -E '(Argument intent|Design guardrails|Discovery cost recurs|Treat user Socratic)' on the file
3. Observe: each phrase appears on at least 2 line numbers (~116-121 and ~127-128 as of incident)
4. Verify the duplicates have slight wording variants (one with '[[wiki-links]]' backticked, one without; one with 'wasn't' vs 'was not')

## Source

Sprint 21 session-reflect, 2026-05-06. The incident itself validates the premise of bd vp-claude-2yk (knowledge-maintainer cannot fix observation duplication via edit_note alone; main-session write_note(overwrite=true) is required). Adjacent: this also surfaced the validation-error-doesn't-roll-back behavior as a separate generalizable BM MCP gotcha.
acceptance_criteria: parallel-agent-orchestration-lessons note has exactly ONE copy of each of the 4 dedicated observations from the incident; a new [gotcha] captures the validation-error-doesn't-roll-back rule; search_notes for each unique phrase returns exactly one match; npm run check passes.
close_reason: Note dedup + new validation-error gotcha applied via main-session write_note(overwrite=true); search_notes verifies exactly 1 instance per phrase; npm run check passes (4/4 stages, exit 0); new [gotcha] cross-references the Design guardrails pattern.

title: Bridge gardener→maintainer fix loop for observation duplication
description:
## The gap

The vp-knowledge maintainer agent's contract (CLAUDE.md): 'All-in-one write agent that acts on audit findings. Auto-fixes structural issues.'

The gardener agent flags observation duplication as a structural issue (Sprint 21 caught crate-rmcp with apparent ~52 observations where ~26 unique exist).

But the maintainer's tool list deliberately excludes write_note and delete_note — and edit_note find_replace cannot reliably remove scattered duplicate observation lines (find_text matches both original and duplicate; targeting one without the other requires position-aware tooling that doesn't exist in BM today).

Result: gardener flags the issue, maintainer tries the fix, hits the wall, user must intervene with main-session write_note(overwrite=true). The audit-driven 'gardener flags → maintainer fixes' workflow breaks at this class of structural issue.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a BM note with deliberately-duplicated observation lines (e.g. write_note then immediately edit_note find_replace to insert duplicate copies of several observation blocks)
2. Run the knowledge-gardener agent — it correctly flags the duplication
3. Invoke the knowledge-maintainer agent and ask it to fix the gardener-flagged duplication
4. Observe: maintainer cannot fix it. edit_note find_replace cannot identify which of the N duplicate lines to remove (find_text matches both original and duplicate; specifying one occurrence requires position-aware tooling). Maintainer reports inability to act and either escalates or no-ops.
5. The user must drop into the main session and use write_note(overwrite=true) with deduplicated content — bypassing the maintainer entirely.

Sprint 21 evidence: crate-rmcp dedup required main-session write_note(overwrite=true). bd remember entry preserves the methodology but does not eliminate the recurring discovery cost.

## Why I initially mis-framed this as 'not a bug'

(Captured for thinking-trail completeness.)

I argued: (1) exclusion is security-oriented; (2) main-session fallback works; (3) single occurrence in 21 sprints. On reflection:

- (1) The maintainer already has edit_note (can replace large chunks via aggressive find_replace) and move_note (just observed updating 14 inbound relations across 8 notes in Sprint 21). Forbidding write_note(overwrite=true) while allowing those is inconsistent on the 'blast radius' axis.
- (2) The fallback works but the discovery cost recurs every occurrence. Future me will see gardener flag → try maintainer → hit wall → read bd remember → switch to main session. Capturing the methodology in bd remember + BM observation makes the friction navigable, not absent.
- (3) Single-occurrence in 21 sprints is misleading. The gardener-maintainer split is recent (post-Sprint 18); this was the first opportunity for the path to surface, not evidence of rarity. Going forward, every gardener-flagged duplication will hit the same wall.

## Implementation options

Option A — New skill: '/dedup-observations <note-identifier>' that internally uses read_note → diff observations → write_note(overwrite=true) with safety wrappers (schema_validate before writing, checksum verification, optional --dry-run preview). The maintainer can invoke it via Skill tool. Encodes dedup logic once instead of improvising it each time. Estimated: medium effort, single-file skill.

Option B — Maintainer-internal pattern: extend the maintainer to handle dedup as a special case via a Skill-tool delegation to /dedup-observations (built per Option A). Smaller change to the maintainer itself.

Option C — Upstream feature request to basic-memory: add a position-aware editing primitive (delete_observation_at_line(N), or dedup_observations() at the MCP level). This is the cleanest fix architecturally — solves the root cause (BM's edit_note is line-text-based, not position-aware) — but is upstream, single-data-point, and would need to be filed against basicmachines-co/basic-memory.

Recommended path: Option A first (encodes the logic in vp-knowledge where we control it), Option B as a follow-up (wires it into the maintainer), Option C as upstream feature request when a second data point lands.

## Sprint 21 evidence and prior captures

- Methodology captured in bd remember: 'vp-knowledge knowledge-maintainer agent excludes write_note and delete_note...'
- Generalizable [gotcha] observation now in BM: engineering/agents/parallel-agent-orchestration-lessons (the operational corollary to the existing [decision] line about excluding irreversible tools)
- RETRO-21.md 'What could improve' section flags the gap

## Out of scope (separate concern)

- The crate-rmcp duplication ambiguity (was the count anomaly real or a counting artifact?) — not investigated this sprint; flagged for second-occurrence trigger.
acceptance_criteria: An audit-flagged observation duplication on an existing BM note can be fixed end-to-end without requiring the user to drop into the main session. Either: (a) a new /dedup-observations skill exists with safety wrappers and is invocable from the maintainer via Skill tool; OR (b) the maintainer agent itself gains a controlled dedup pathway with equivalent guardrails; OR (c) basic-memory ships a position-aware editing primitive that lets edit_note solve dedup natively (with corresponding maintainer prompt update). Verification: re-run the gardener on a deliberately-duplicated test note; gardener flags it; maintainer fixes it; gardener re-runs and reports zero duplicates — all without main-session intervention.
notes:
RECONSIDERATION 2026-05-06 (during split work on parallel-agent-orchestration-lessons):

The original 'keep write_note out of maintainer; user does it in main session' verdict from the dual-review (vp-claude-95b/sqw) conflated two arguments:
1. **Oversight argument** — user eyes on the diff before destructive writes
2. **Capability argument** — exclude the tool because of mistake risk

Argument 1 is a *behavior* (preview-then-write); argument 2 is a *capability* (tool access). They are separable. A maintainer with write_note REQUIRED to preview-and-confirm preserves oversight while gaining efficiency.

The technical efficiency argument is significant: a structural fix involving 10+ observation moves requires 20+ edit_note calls, which hits BM's documented SQLite serialization limit AND leaves non-atomic state if any call mid-batch fails. One write_note(overwrite=true) is faster, lock-safer, and atomic. This session's catalog-note structural cleanup (10 moved observations + 1 added pattern + example generalization) was done as a single write_note(overwrite=true) for exactly this reason.

PROPOSED resolution path (revisit when this bead is ready for action):
- Adopt the architect's Option B from the dual-review (was rejected): add write_note to maintainer tools list with a STRICT workflow gate requiring read_note → preview reconstruction → user confirms diff → write_note(overwrite=true). The gate is workflow prose, but enforceable: the maintainer must NEVER call write_note without first surfacing a preview, and the autonomy rules classify it as confirm-required.
- OR: architect's Option C (vp-dedup-observations sub-skill wrapping write_note) — isolates the destructive verb behind a single-purpose wrapper. Heavier (one more SKILL.md) but makes the boundary explicit in code rather than prose.

Both options should be re-scoped against vp-claude-95b (escalation subsection) — if Option B/C lands, the escalation subsection becomes much smaller (mostly just delete_note remains as a main-session-only operation).
close_reason: User decision 2026-07-03: prevention (sqw, closed same session) is sufficient. Cure-half (new dedup skill / maintainer write access / upstream fix) not worth building given b74's reclassification of the underlying duplication phenomenon as often a transient echo, not real corruption.

title: Argument parser: handle bare github.com/<org>/<repo> URLs in /package-intel and /tool-intel
description:
Currently /package-intel requires an ecosystem prefix (npm:, crate:, go:, etc.). Users frequently paste bare GitHub URLs like 'github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk' instead. The skill's project-context fallback (go.mod → go ecosystem) silently misroutes for non-Go GitHub URLs.

Sprint 21 example: user pasted 'github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk' AND 'github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk'. Naive parsing would have produced go-github.com-modelcontextprotocol-rust-sdk (wrong ecosystem, wrong name) and go-github.com-modelcontextprotocol-typescript-sdk (wrong everything; the existing note is at npm-@modelcontextprotocol-sdk).

Required deeper reasoning to route correctly to crate:rmcp and the existing TS SDK note. Skill grammar should help users avoid this.

Improvement options:
1. Step 0.5 in both /package-intel and /tool-intel: detect 'github.com/<org>/<repo>' paths, probe registries (crates.io, npm, pkg.go.dev) by repo name, suggest the right ecosystem
2. Heuristic on repo naming: '-sdk' suffix is unreliable (e.g., go-sdk vs rust-sdk vs typescript-sdk); registry probe is more authoritative
3. Always-error-out-and-prompt approach: 'ambiguous — please prefix with crate:/npm:/go:/...' rather than silent misrouting

Acceptance: pasting 'github.com/<org>/<repo>' produces correctly-routed note OR explicit 'ambiguous' prompt; never silent misrouting to wrong ecosystem.

Source: Sprint 21 retrospective (RETRO-21.md) 'What could improve'.
acceptance_criteria: Both /package-intel and /tool-intel handle bare github.com/<org>/<repo> URLs without silent misrouting. Either correctly identify the ecosystem via registry probe, or emit a clear 'ambiguous — please prefix' message. Tests cover at least: a Rust crate at github.com/.../rust-sdk → routes to crate:; a TS package at github.com/.../typescript-sdk → routes to npm:; an unambiguous Go module → routes to go:; an ambiguous case → prompts.

title: Reference Raindrop update_bookmarks silent-fail rules from raindrop skills + agent prose
description:
## Why

The two update_bookmarks silent-fail combos (add_tags+remove_tags returns "Unknown error" silent fail; add_tags+collection_id returns success but applies move only, drops tags — lying success) are captured as [gotcha] observations on main/engineering/governance/raindrop-tag-health-audit-2026-04-06 but NOT referenced from skills/raindrop-triage/SKILL.md, skills/tag-sync/SKILL.md, or agents/raindrop-gardener.md. ## What

2. skills/tag-sync/SKILL.md (any tag-mutation step)
3. agents/raindrop-gardener.md (recommended-call section)

Source: Sprint 21 wave-2 multi-agent research.

title: AGENTS.md profile:minimal marker disagrees with full-profile body content
description:
## Why

AGENTS.md line 39 BEGIN marker says "v:1 profile:minimal hash:ca08a54f" but lines 59-83 contain full-profile content (Session Completion section with bd dolt push and MANDATORY WORKFLOW). Per Sprint 21 wave-2 DeepWiki research on steveyegge/beads (internal/templates/agents/render.go + cmd/bd/init_agent.go), the next bd init invocation will recompute the hash against the minimal template, detect mismatch, and call ReplaceSection to overwrite — silently shrinking the block and dropping the workflow content.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. cd /Users/pelle/Sites/ai/vp-claude
2. Note that AGENTS.md line 39 begins "<!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION v:1 profile:minimal hash:ca08a54f -->"
3. Note that lines 59-83 contain the full-profile MANDATORY WORKFLOW section (Session Completion + bd dolt push)
4. Run bd init (or any subcommand that triggers the agents-file refresh)
5. Observe: ReplaceSection rewrites lines 39-84 against the minimal template, silently dropping the workflow content

## Resolution Options

(a) Re-render with bd init --agents-profile=full to align the BEGIN marker with the full body content. Per profile-precedence rule (full never downgrades to minimal), this is durable.
(b) Move Session Completion content outside the BEGIN/END markers (above line 84) so it lives in the user-authored zone.

title: Evaluate UPSTREAM-deepwiki.md for research-source friction
description:
## Why

Sprint 19's /package-intel run on go:github.com/timakin/bodyclose hit hallucination-class wrong answers from DeepWiki (returned info about noctx and go-critic when asked about timakin/bodyclose). This is a pattern, not a one-off:

- Small/personal repos are poorly indexed
- DeepWiki may return info about a *different* repo with similar name
- Failure mode is worse than empty results — confident misinformation requires verification effort

Currently no UPSTREAM-deepwiki.md exists. The friction is observable across multiple research sessions but isn't tracked anywhere durable.

## What

1. Decide: (a) start UPSTREAM-deepwiki.md, (b) fold into a generic UPSTREAM-research-tools.md, or (c) skip (DeepWiki is third-party we have no engagement path with).
2. If (a) or (b): log the bodyclose conflation case + add the generic "DeepWiki returns wrong-repo info for niche repos" pattern.
3. Cross-link from BM tool catalog where the gh-as-fallback pattern was just added.

## Notes

The mitigation (use gh api as third research source by default) is already in place — Sprint 19 captured that as a [pattern] in the BM tool catalog. This bead is purely about whether the friction itself deserves an UPSTREAM tracker file.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision recorded: (a) start UPSTREAM-deepwiki.md, (b) fold into a generic UPSTREAM-research-tools.md, or (c) skip with documented trigger to revisit
- If (a) or (b): bodyclose conflation case logged as a Bug entry + a generic "DeepWiki returns wrong-repo info for niche repos" pattern entry exists
- If (c) skip: rationale captured in this bead's notes (e.g., "no engagement path with DeepWiki maintainers" or "gh fallback in vp-claude-9zi mitigates sufficiently")
- Cross-link from BM tool catalog observation about gh-as-fallback verified or added
- vp-claude-9zi remains the active mitigation regardless of decision
close_reason: Decision: option (c) SKIP with documented revisit trigger. Rationale: (1) no engagement path with DeepWiki maintainers (closed-source vendor; filing UPSTREAM entries against unreachable vendors produces bookkeeping debt without recovery levers); (2) vp-claude-9zi (closed in same sprint) ships the working mitigation in skill prose — both /package-intel Step 3a and /tool-intel Step 3a now carry hallucination caveats with reference-file fallback. Active mitigation present, no UPSTREAM tracking needed. REVISIT TRIGGER: if a 2nd DeepWiki hallucination occurs in any /package-intel or /tool-intel run within the next 4 sprints, re-evaluate options (a) start UPSTREAM-deepwiki.md or (b) fold into UPSTREAM-research-tools.md. Cross-link: vp-claude-9zi remains the active mitigation; bm tool catalog [pattern] 'gh api is the structural fallback when DeepWiki and Context7 produce unreliable or empty output for a target repo' captures the durable rule.

title: Re-evaluate go_module Tier C schema fields when N≥5 notes
description:
## Why

Sprint 19 expanded the go_module schema with Tier A+B fields (security, api, platform, history, reference, license, author, created_by, contrasts_with). Three Tier C candidates were deferred:

- dependency (33%, single-source: claude-gomod) — overlaps with depends_on relation
- protocol (33%, single-source: sideterm) — niche
- insight (33%, single-source: sideterm) — generic catch-all

Skill rule (>=25% threshold) technically permits adding all three, but with single-note evidence the additions would just bake in noise. Re-run /schema-evolve go_module when N>=5 go_module notes exist to see if any Tier C field has graduated from single-source.

## What

1. Wait for go_module note count to reach 5+
2. Run /schema-evolve go_module
3. Apply Tier C fields with multi-source evidence; defer those that remain single-source
acceptance_criteria:
- Trigger condition met: go_module note count >=5 (currently 3 as of 2026-05-04)
- /schema-evolve go_module run, drift output reviewed against updated note distribution
- For each Tier C candidate (dependency, protocol, insight): added to schema if usage spans >=2 distinct notes (multi-source evidence); deferred again if still single-source
- /schema-evolve dual-syncs both BM schema/go-module note and schemas/go_module.md if changes applied
- schema_validate(note_type="go_module") passes 0 errors / 0 warnings against all go_module notes after any changes
notes: TRIGGER FIRED 2026-07-03 (Haiku recon + Opus validation): go_module notes grew from 3 (2026-05-04, when this bead was filed) to 17 (2026-07-03) -- well past the N>=5 revival trigger. schemas/go_module.md still carries no Tier C field categorization. title: Research PostCompact hook as PreCompact replacement
description: Investigate whether to adopt PostCompact (v2.1.76+) as a REPLACEMENT for the now-retired PreCompact hook (PreCompact was retired in the Apr 2026 hook-cleanup sprint; PostCompact would be a different mechanism, not a companion). Open questions: (a) what fields does the compact_summary input carry -- full summary text or structured object? (b) does the underdocumented 'if'-style filter syntax (per gap-fill Q7 in the hook-audit) work for skip-conditions? (c) does the post-compaction context still allow MCP write tool calls, or are we in the same 'Haiku without MCP' trap that bit prompt-hooks (RETRO-02)? Validate by writing a minimal posttest.sh that just dumps stdin to /tmp/, hooking it as PostCompact, and triggering compaction. Decide based on observed input shape and whether compact_summary is useful enough to warrant resurrecting compaction-time reflection. Source: hook-audit B3, deferred per Q7.
acceptance_criteria:
- Minimal posttest.sh hook script written and registered as a PostCompact handler
- Compaction triggered (via /compact or natural cliff) with stdin captured to /tmp/
- Three open questions answered with concrete observations from the captured stdin:
  - (a) compact_summary input shape — full summary text vs structured object
  - (b) `if`-style filter syntax behavior in PostCompact context
  - (c) MCP write-tool availability — full handler vs Haiku-no-MCP trap (RETRO-02 mechanism)
- Decision recorded in this bead's notes: adopt PostCompact for a specific use case, defer with explicit revival trigger, or reject with rationale
close_reason:
Closed as won't-do per 2026-05-05 substrate research + design decision (user-confirmed).

Substrate IS clear (PostCompact v2.1.76+, type:"command", plain-text compact_summary) per code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and DeepWiki against anthropics/claude-code CHANGELOG. But the original PreCompact retirement rationale ("low-quality changelog noise") applies equally to PostCompact's compact_summary — it's also a Claude-generated summary with the same noise floor. PostCompact + type:"mcp_tool" was considered and rejected (mcp_tool invokes one named tool with templated input; cannot do conditional capture decisions).

Substrate findings preserved in BM at engineering/tooling/claude-code-plugin-mechanics for future revival.

Re-open trigger: a session demonstrates a concrete need for compaction-time hooks that the existing SessionStart hook (which can react after compaction completes via session restart) cannot satisfy.

title: Wiki-link colon anti-pattern detector at write time
description: Add a PostToolUse(write_note|edit_note) hook that flags colon-form wiki-links like [[npm:foo]] and emits a corrective additionalContext recommending hyphen form [[npm-foo]]. Two stdin shapes to handle: write_note carries tool_input.content (full note body); edit_note find_replace mode carries tool_input.find_replace[].replace_text (array of replacement segments). Regex: \[\[(npm|crate|pypi|go|composer|gem|brew|cask|action|docker|vscode|person):. Either extend post-bm-write-validate.sh (must merge with existing schema-validate additionalContext into ONE JSON object -- Claude Code reads only the first) or add as a sibling script with its own hooks.json entry. Estimated +55 LOC, medium-high risk. The knowledge-gardener already catches this in periodic audits (per MEMORY.md known-issues 2026-04-12) -- this bead is for write-time prevention. Source: hook-audit P2-8, deferred per Q6.
acceptance_criteria:
- New (or extended) PostToolUse hook detects colon-form wiki-links matching `\[\[(npm|crate|pypi|go|composer|gem|brew|cask|action|docker|vscode|person):` in:
  - write_note tool_input.content
  - edit_note tool_input.find_replace[].replace_text array entries
- Hook emits corrective additionalContext recommending hyphen form (e.g. [[npm-foo]] not [[npm:foo]])
- Single-JSON-object output contract preserved — merges with schema-validate additionalContext into ONE object if extending the existing hook
- Integration test added in scripts/check-hooks.mjs covering at least one colon-form positive case and one hyphen-form clean-pass case
notes: Research update 2026-05-05 (multi-agent triangulation): confirmed implementation path — extend EXISTING post-bm-write-validate.sh as a SECOND condition branch in the SAME JSON object output, NOT a new hook entry. This preserves the single-JSON-object contract (multiple hook entries with overlapping matchers run as independent processes; combined script is also more efficient — one stdin parse, one process spawn). Regex: \[\[(npm|crate|go|composer|pypi|gem|brew|cask|action|docker|vscode|gh): against tool_input.content and tool_input.find_replace[].replacement (or .replace_text). Add check-hooks.mjs integration test asserting both schema-validate reminder AND wiki-link warning appear in additionalContext when both fire.

title: Add note-size coherence audit to knowledge-gardener for notes >40KB
description:
Add an audit step to knowledge-gardener.md: for notes >40KB, list ### heading count + extracted subject phrases; flag for human review when >2 distinct subjects are detected. Output is ADVISORY — never auto-split. Splitting is editorial decomposition that requires constructing new conceptual abstractions; automating risks the structural equivalent of the duplicate-observation incident.

Threshold rationale: 40KB is the point where coherence-audit cost (~1 min human attention) is justified by hit rate. Below 40KB, hit rate is low. Above 80KB, BM read_note pagination kicks in and LLM context cost grows non-trivial — strong signal at that point.

Subject-drift signals to detect:
1. Multiple top-level ## headings (beyond Observations + Relations)
2. ### subsections appearing AFTER ## Relations (structural misplacement)
3. Tag drift: cohesive set → multiple distinct sets
4. Cross-reference asymmetry: subsections cited mostly from outside the note

Do NOT: auto-split, add lint warnings, put splitting in maintainer autonomy rules, treat as regular maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: agents/knowledge-gardener.md has a new audit step (numbered, integrated into existing flow) that detects notes >40KB, counts ### headings, extracts subject phrases, flags >2 distinct subjects for human review. Output is advisory only — no auto-action. Threshold-table documented in workflow prose. The maintainer agent does NOT gain auto-split capability. npm run check passes.
notes:
Scope narrowed (2026-05-06 user decision): KEEP MCP-only, accept partial coverage. Don't expand gardener's Bash-permission boundary for this feature.

Gardener-3 audit confirmed pure-MCP size discovery is impractical at ~1,043 notes (no aggregate-size endpoint in BM; per-note read_note doesn't scale). The audit step should:
- Run only on high-likelihood directories (engineering/agents/, engineering/concepts/, etc.) via list_directory + read_note(output_format='json')
- Document the partial-coverage caveat in the gardener step prose so users know it's a sample, not exhaustive
- Defer to manual eyes-on-it review when notes feel large but aren't in audited dirs

Out of scope: filesystem find -size +40k expansion (would require PreToolUse hook allowlist exception). The strict no-Bash gardener boundary is preserved; the gap-coverage cost is acceptable.

title: Cask-to-service auto-linking in knowledge-maintainer
description:
Casks that install services (Warp, Raycast, Obsidian, Docker Desktop) should auto-link to corresponding service:* notes. Detection rule infers from cask artifact metadata.

IMPLEMENTATION (revised 2026-05-05 after multi-agent research):

NO schema change needed for brew_cask. Auto-linking is *inference at audit time*, not a *captured field*. The Homebrew MCP (mcp__homebrew__info <cask>) returns the artifact taxonomy in plain text under `==> Artifacts` with type labels:
  Ghostty.app (App)
  ghostty.1 (Manpage)
  ghostty.bash (Bash Completion)

Parse the (App) lines (regex `^(.+\.app)\s+\(App\)$`), strip `.app`, fuzzy-match to existing service-* notes by name (e.g., `Ghostty.app` → `service-ghostty` if it exists). Existing cask notes (e.g., cask-ghostty) don't currently store artifacts — and shouldn't, because the data is freely available from mcp__homebrew__info on demand.

Ontology decision: use `relates_to` from existing picoschema vocabulary (post-0.29.1 canonicalization sweep). Don't invent a new `installs` verb until iterative use establishes the need.

Spawned from Homebrew MCP integration plan (vp-claude-baz). YAGNI-revive: when user manually creates a third "cask installs a service" cross-link.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ontology decision recorded in knowledge-maintainer prose: relation verb `relates_to` (existing picoschema vocabulary, no new field, no schema change)
- Detection rule implemented: parse `==> Artifacts` section from mcp__homebrew__info, extract (App) entries, fuzzy-match to existing service-* notes
- No schema change to brew_cask — artifacts are inferred at audit time, not captured
- Auto-link applied during knowledge-maintainer audits with user-confirmation gate per match (per the content-change rule — this is a content-level edit, not a structural fix)
